articles.headline: Two Indian seafarers missing after ship struck in Black Sea
articles.summary: Two Indian sailors are missing after their Palau-flagged cargo vessel, MV AGN Ragnar, was attacked by three drones off the coast of Ukraine in the Black Sea. The vessel had 10 crew members, including three Indians. While one Indian sailor was rescued by the Romanian Coast Guard, search operations continue for the other two missing crew members amid a drone threat in the region.

articles.headline: Four workers killed in molten metal blast at Assam factory
articles.summary: At least four workers were killed and two others injured in an explosion at a metal processing unit in Assam's Cachar district. The incident occurred at the Kade Global Infrastructure LLP plant when molten metal spilled on workers. Local residents and family members have demanded a thorough investigation into the blast, which is the second such incident at the facility since 2024.

articles.headline: Water supply hit in parts of Delhi due to Munak Canal leak
articles.summary: Water supply was disrupted across North, West, and South-West Delhi after a leak was detected in the Munak Canal. The Delhi Jal Board (DJB) reported that several water treatment plants were affected, leading to shortages in residential areas including Rohini and Dwarka. Repair work is underway, and supply is expected to be restored gradually over the next 48 hours.

articles.headline: Cabinet Secretary asks bureaucrats to shed 'playing safe' approach
articles.summary: New Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan has urged senior bureaucrats to move away from 'playing safe' and avoid excessive centralisation. In a communication to Union ministries, he stressed the need for a culture of trust and delegation of power to junior levels to speed up government decision-making and prevent the clogging of the governance system.

articles.headline: Three killed as double-decker bus overturns in UP's Sambhal
articles.summary: Three passengers were killed and over 25 injured when a private double-decker bus overturned in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal district. The bus, traveling from Bahraich to Punjab, reportedly hit a divider and flipped after the driver fell asleep at the wheel. The injured were shifted to local hospitals, and a case has been registered against the driver for negligence.

articles.headline: One dead, 26 injured in private bus accident in Kerala
articles.summary: One person died and 26 others were injured after a private bus skidded and overturned on a highway in Kerala's Malappuram district. The bus, traveling from Kozhikode to Thrissur, reportedly lost control on a rain-slicked road. Police have registered a case and are investigating whether the accident was caused by speeding or poor road conditions.

articles.headline: Delhi man electrocuted while connecting water pump wiring
articles.summary: A 39-year-old man died of electrocution in south Delhi's Tigri area while attempting to connect the electrical wiring of a water pump to a tanker. Preliminary investigations suggest a short circuit in the wiring led to the fatal accident. The Delhi Jal Board clarified that neither the tanker nor the pump belonged to the department or its authorized vendors.

articles.headline: Parsvnath deposits ₹2.9 cr, seeks unfreezing of bank accounts
articles.summary: Real estate developer Parsvnath Hessa Developers Pvt Ltd informed the Supreme Court that it has deposited ₹2.9 crore toward dues for home-buyers in Gurugram. The company sought the lifting of bank account freezes and other coercive actions to allow it to fulfill pending liabilities. The court will examine the compliance of the developer in the next hearing.

articles.headline: Assam residents declared foreigners get second chance at citizenship
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that 27 Assam residents declared foreigners by tribunals must be given a second chance to prove their citizenship. The court emphasized that citizenship disputes must be decided through a process that satisfies constitutional standards of fairness. The ruling offers a lifeline to several families who were declared foreigners in ex-parte proceedings.

articles.headline: US court upholds block on Trump mail-in voting order
articles.summary: A US federal appeals court has upheld a ruling blocking a move to restrict the use of mail-in ballots. The decision prevents an order that would have allowed states to create 'state citizenship lists' to identify and remove potential non-citizens from voting rolls. Critics argued the policy was politically motivated and aimed at suppressing valid votes ahead of the upcoming elections.

articles.headline: DCs will be held accountable for exam paper leaks: Karnataka CM
articles.summary: Karnataka Deputy CM DK Shivakumar warned district administrations that Deputy Commissioners would be held directly responsible for any question paper leaks or exam malpractice. The warning comes as the state prepares for a series of large-scale recruitment exams. The government has ordered the installation of CCTV cameras and police oversight at all examination centers to ensure transparency.

articles.headline: Ex-KPSC chief faces probe in recruitment fraud case
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has ordered a fresh investigation into former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar over allegations of fraud in the recruitment of veterinary officers. The probe follows a complaint regarding favoritism and the manipulation of exam scores. This is the latest in a series of scandals to hit the state's public service recruitment commission.

articles.headline: Man dragged on car bonnet over rash driving argument in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A cab driver in Bengaluru was arrested for dragging a man on his car's bonnet for nearly a kilometer following an argument over rash driving. The victim had confronted the driver for driving recklessly, which led to the confrontation. The driver sped away with the man clinging to the bonnet before being stopped by local residents and police. The victim suffered minor injuries.

articles.headline: Deep depression over Bay of Bengal may turn into cyclonic storm
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) has warned that a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm within 24 hours. The system is moving northwestwards toward the North Andhra coast. Heavy rain and gale-force winds are expected, and fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea until Wednesday.

articles.headline: Two dead, one injured in explosion at TN firecracker factory
articles.summary: An explosion at a firecracker manufacturing unit in Tamil Nadu's Virudhunagar district killed two people and left one critically injured. The unit was reportedly operating without a valid license in a residential area. Preliminary investigations suggest friction during the mixing of chemicals caused the blast. Police have registered a case against the owner of the illegal facility.

articles.headline: Vijay's 'last film' Jana Nayagan collects over ₹170 cr in 3 days
articles.summary: Tamil actor Vijay's latest film, 'Jana Nayagan', has grossed over ₹170 crore worldwide within three days of its release. Marketed as his final film before a full-time entry into politics, the movie saw massive openings across Tamil Nadu and Kerala. Despite mixed reviews from critics, strong fan sentiment and record advance bookings have fueled its box-office success.

articles.headline: India steadily moving towards self-reliance in defence: PM Modi
articles.summary: During his 'Mann Ki Baat' address, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted India's progress in achieving 'Aatmanirbharta' (self-reliance) in the defence sector. He cited the success of the Pinaka rocket system and the BrahMos missile as evidence of India's growing domestic manufacturing capabilities. Modi also encouraged citizens to support local products and participate in the 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign.

articles.headline: Tej Pratap Yadav sent to judicial custody in Bihar
articles.summary: Former Bihar minister Tej Pratap Yadav was sent to 14-day judicial custody by a Patna court for his alleged role in inciting violent protests over the NEET paper leak case. Yadav was arrested after several students and political activists clashed with police during a march. He has denied the charges, claiming the action is a political conspiracy by the state government.

articles.headline: Assam deluge intensified by mining and weak embankments
articles.summary: A detailed report on the recent Assam floods highlights that excessive coal mining, weak river embankments, and the loss of natural wetlands have worsened the annual deluge. Environmentalists noted that deforestation in hilly areas has led to increased siltation in rivers, reducing their carrying capacity. The report calls for urgent restoration of wetlands and stricter mining regulations to mitigate future floods.

articles.headline: Arunachal minister dismisses claims of Chinese intrusion in state
articles.summary: Arunachal Pradesh Home Minister Mama Natung dismissed reports of a Chinese military intrusion in the Anjaw district. Natung stated that the Indian Army and ITBP maintain a strict vigil along the border and no such activity has been observed. The statement follows social media rumors suggesting that Chinese troops had set up camps inside Indian territory.

articles.headline: Vietnam ship sinks in South China Sea, 17 crew missing
articles.summary: A multinational search operation is underway in the South China Sea after a Vietnamese cargo vessel sank during a storm. All 17 crew members on board are reported missing. The ship was carrying over 2,000 tons of coal and sank rapidly after being hit by heavy waves. Rescuers from China and Vietnam are coordinating efforts, though bad weather is hampering the search.

articles.headline: Price wars pinch IT services sector as AI adoption rises
articles.summary: India's $300-billion IT services industry is facing intense price pressure as clients demand lower billing rates for projects where AI is used to improve productivity. Major firms like TCS and Infosys are navigating a shift from traditional labor-intensive models to AI-driven automation. This trend is impacting profit margins as companies compete for high-value digital transformation contracts.

articles.headline: iPhone shipment growth in India slows after four years
articles.summary: Apple's iPhone shipments in India fell by 3% year-on-year in the April-June quarter, marking the first decline in four years. Market analysts attribute the slowdown to consumers delaying purchases in anticipation of the upcoming iPhone 17 series. Despite the quarterly dip, Apple continues to view India as a major growth engine and is expanding its local manufacturing operations.

articles.headline: FM Sitharaman says regulation should be guardrails, not tollgates
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that government regulation in the business sector should serve as protective guardrails rather than restrictive tollgates. Speaking at a business leadership summit, she emphasized the need for a trust-based regulatory framework to encourage innovation and investment. She highlighted recent decriminalization of minor business lapses as a step toward this goal.

articles.headline: RBI Keeps Repo Rate Unchanged at 6.5 Percent
articles.summary: The RBI kept the benchmark repo rate unchanged at 6.5% for the seventh consecutive meeting. The Monetary Policy Committee aims to align inflation with the 4% target while supporting economic growth. Governor Shaktikanta Das emphasized a "withdrawal of accommodation" stance to ensure price stability amid global uncertainties.

articles.headline: India Manufacturing PMI Reaches 16-Year High in March
articles.summary: India's manufacturing sector showed robust growth in March as the HSBC PMI rose to 59.1 from 56.9 in February. This marks the highest level in 16 years, driven by strong domestic and export demand. Companies reported the sharpest rise in production and new orders since late 2020, leading to significant increases in hiring and purchasing activity.

articles.headline: Government Targets Rs 7.5 Lakh Crore Borrowing in First Half
articles.summary: The Union Government plans to borrow Rs 7.5 lakh crore through dated securities during the April-September period of FY25. This constitutes roughly 53% of the total annual gross borrowing target of Rs 14.13 lakh crore. The borrowing schedule includes 26 weekly auctions, aimed at funding the fiscal deficit while managing market liquidity and interest rate volatility.

articles.headline: Adani Green Becomes First Firm With 10,000 MW Renewable Capacity
articles.summary: Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) has surpassed 10,000 megawatts of operational renewable energy capacity, a first for any Indian company. The milestone includes a massive 2,000 MW solar capacity addition at the Khavda renewable energy park in Gujarat. AGEL aims to reach 45,000 MW capacity by 2030, contributing significantly to India's decarbonization goals.

articles.headline: Vistara to Reduce Daily Flights Amidst Pilot Shortage
articles.summary: Vistara is scaling back its flight operations following widespread disruptions caused by pilot unavailability. The airline faced over 100 cancellations and numerous delays as pilots protested revised salary structures and fatigue. Management is working to stabilize the schedule by reducing daily frequencies to create more buffer capacity in its crew rosters.

articles.headline: Apple to Allow Default Navigation App Changes in EU Market
articles.summary: Apple will permit European Union users to set third-party navigation apps as defaults on iPhones by late 2024. This change complies with the Digital Markets Act (DMA), aimed at curbing the dominance of tech giants. Additionally, Apple is developing a more user-friendly way for consumers to transfer data to non-Apple devices to improve platform interoperability.

articles.headline: Indirect Tax Collections Surpass Revised Estimates for FY24
articles.summary: India's indirect tax collections, including GST and customs, have exceeded the revised budget estimates for the 2023-24 fiscal year. The growth is attributed to strong domestic consumption and improved tax administration. While the final figures are being tallied, early data suggests a significant surplus, providing the government more fiscal room to manage the deficit.

articles.headline: Centre scraps ₹10,000-crore ATF fund as airlines skip MoU deadline
articles.summary: The Union government has discontinued its planned ₹10,000-crore aviation turbine fuel (ATF) Price Stabilisation Fund. The decision came after no domestic airlines signed the mandatory tripartite MoU with oil marketing companies and the Ministry of Civil Aviation by the prescribed deadline. The fund was intended to protect airlines from global fuel price volatility.

articles.headline: Small truckers struggle for survival amid rising costs and low rates
articles.summary: Small truck operators in India are facing a severe crisis due to rising diesel prices, high loan repayments, and stagnant freight rates. Industry estimates suggest that over 75% of transport operators own five or fewer trucks, and many are now struggling to meet operating costs, leading to fears of widespread business closures and limited pricing power.

articles.headline: Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh set for inauguration on August 1
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Bhogapuram greenfield airport near Visakhapatnam on August 1. The event will feature traditional Dimsa dance performances by 13,000 tribal artists from the Araku region. Developed by the GMR Group, the airport is expected to significantly boost regional connectivity and tourism in North Andhra.

articles.headline: Attacks on Red Sea infrastructure pose risk to India's crude imports
articles.summary: Crude oil imports from Russia face renewed risks due to Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian Black Sea ports and Houthi attacks in the Red Sea. While Indian refiners have reconfigured sourcing, these tensions could inflate freight costs and insurance premiums, potentially impacting the significant discounts India currently enjoys on Russian crude supplies.

articles.headline: Margin Trading Facility book reaches ₹1.43 lakh crore despite slower growth
articles.summary: The industry's Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book touched a record high of ₹1.43 lakh crore on July 22, 2026, driven by retail investor interest. However, the monthly pace of growth has slowed to 5.1% in July compared to higher rates earlier in the year. Analysts attribute the cooling trend to higher transaction taxes and more cautious investor sentiment.

articles.headline: EPFO identifies 1.13 lakh dormant accounts for automatic small-value refunds
articles.summary: The Ministry of Labour and Employment has identified 1.13 lakh inactive Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) accounts holding less than ₹1,000. Using a new 'penny drop' verification system linked to Aadhaar, the EPFO aims to automatically credit these unclaimed funds to subscribers' active bank accounts by August, reducing the need for manual claims.

articles.headline: PM Modi skips NEET controversy in latest Mann Ki Baat address
articles.summary: In his first Mann Ki Baat broadcast of his third term, Prime Minister Narendra Modi focused on space achievements, environmental conservation, and the 'Catch the Rain' campaign. Notably, the address did not mention the ongoing NEET-UG paper leak controversy or the related student protests, focusing instead on grassroots success stories and national pride.

articles.headline: T+0 settlement rollout delayed as brokers struggle with technical readiness
articles.summary: The plan to transition Indian stock markets to a T+0 (same-day) settlement cycle has been delayed. While stock exchanges were prepared to expand the pilot, the Ministry of Finance has put the move on hold as many brokers lack the necessary back-end infrastructure and real-time funding capabilities to handle instant settlements across a wider range of stocks.

articles.headline: KIMS stock shows bullish trend with potential for further gains
articles.summary: Shares of Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences (KIMS) have entered a long-term uptrend, according to technical analysis. After hitting a record high and a minor correction, the stock has formed a bullish 'morning star' pattern. Analysts suggest a target price of ₹875 with a stop-loss at ₹760, indicating potential for a fresh leg of rally.

articles.headline: FM Nirmala Sitharaman urges I-T department to improve service for commoners
articles.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has called on the Income Tax Department to focus on the benefit of common citizens. She expressed disappointment over delays in constructing department buildings on government-allotted land, emphasizing that efficient infrastructure and a proactive approach are key to providing better public service and resolving grievances.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu extends Seventh State Finance Commission's tenure by four months
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has extended the tenure of the Seventh State Finance Commission until December 31, 2026. The commission, chaired by C.P. Singh, is tasked with reviewing the financial position of local bodies and recommending the distribution of state tax revenues. The extension aims to allow for a thorough examination of rural and urban local body needs.

articles.headline: Strong Q1 direct tax collections reflect India's economic resilience
articles.summary: Direct tax collections for the first quarter of FY2026-27 have shown significant growth, with a 22% rise in corporate tax and 16% in advance tax. This trend, despite rising costs in some sectors, suggests broad-based demand and improved tax compliance. The buoyancy provides a fiscal cushion for government expenditure amid global disruptions.

articles.headline: Analysis of the Modi government's administrative style and parliamentary challenges
articles.summary: Commentator TCA Srinivasa Raghavan analyzes the Modi government's governance style, noting a gap between political strength and administrative responsiveness. He suggests that while the government has managed political crises well, it faces challenges in addressing systemic issues like the NEET controversy and middle-class frustrations through more honest administration.

articles.headline: China overhauls higher education to prepare for AI-driven labor shifts
articles.summary: China is aggressively restructuring its university curriculum to build capacity in areas like semiconductors, AI, and green energy. The move aims to address high youth unemployment and ensure a talent pipeline that can withstand the 'AI shock,' shifting focus from humanities to high-tech manufacturing and strategic technology sectors.

articles.headline: New generation of Lutyens' Delhi elite embraces social media for influence
articles.summary: A new wave of youth-focused leaders in Delhi is utilizing platforms like Instagram and X to build political brands. Unlike the polished PR of the past, this approach uses irony, sarcasm, and spontaneous engagement to connect with voters, marking a shift in how the political establishment communicates and manages its public image.

articles.headline: Dr. Cyriac Abby Philips' book 'The Liver Doctor' challenges alternative medicine
articles.summary: A review of 'The Liver Doctor' by Dr. Cyriac Abby Philips highlights his mission to debunk myths surrounding liver health and 'miracle' herbal cures. The book provides clinical insights into liver injuries caused by unregulated supplements and advocates for evidence-based medical practices despite facing significant social media pushback and lawsuits.

articles.headline: New biography explores D.K. Shivakumar's rise as Congress's crisis manager
articles.summary: Rasheed Kidwai's book, 'D.K. Shivakumar: Congress’s Kingmaker', provides a portrait of the Karnataka Deputy CM's political journey. The biography examines his role in securing the party's interests, his electoral strategies, and his rise from a rural background to becoming one of India's wealthiest and most influential politicians.

articles.headline: India-UK trade agreement to boost domestic auto-parts manufacturing sector
articles.summary: The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) is expected to significantly benefit India's automotive components industry. By integrating global supply chains and facilitating technology transfers, the pact aims to increase exports, which currently stand at $24 billion, and strengthen India's position as a competitive manufacturing hub.

articles.headline: Premium formats and mega hits drive record post-pandemic cinema revenue
articles.summary: The Indian box office has seen a historic recovery in H1 2026, driven by big-budget spectacles and a surge in demand for premium formats like IMAX and Director’s Cut. Multiplex chains are increasingly investing in luxury seating and advanced technology to attract audiences willing to pay higher prices for an enhanced cinematic experience.

articles.headline: Modern brands use 'sleuth marketing' to build curiosity and luxury status
articles.summary: A new branding strategy focuses on creating mystery and requiring consumer effort to 'discover' products. By using minimalist packaging and unconventional retail placements, brands like Teenage Engineering and Fishwife are successfully building cult followings and high-end appeal among 'in-the-know' consumers who value exclusivity and design.

articles.headline: India's booming 'weekend economy' presents new opportunities for urban retail
articles.summary: Consumer spending in urban India is increasingly concentrated on weekends, with up to 61.5% of weekly discretionary expenditure occurring on Saturdays and Sundays. This shift is driving demand for festive-themed retail, street events, and late-night shopping, prompting city planners to consider pedestrian-friendly zones to boost economic activity.

articles.headline: Tata Steel explores EASyMelt technology to reduce coke use in steelmaking
articles.summary: Tata Steel is testing its 'EASyMelt' technology, which uses an electrically assisted syngas smelter to reduce coke consumption in blast furnaces. The process could potentially cut coke usage by 50% and significantly lower carbon emissions without requiring the complete replacement of existing steel-making infrastructure, aiding the transition to green steel.

articles.headline: Researchers develop borophene-based additive to improve castor oil lubrication
articles.summary: Scientists at the Institute of Advanced Study in Science and Technology have found that borophene, a 2D nanomaterial, can significantly improve the lubrication properties of castor oil. Adding just 0.1% borophene reduces friction by 42%, potentially leading to greener and more efficient biolubricants for industrial and automotive use.

articles.headline: Researchers develop organic electrode to accelerate sodium-ion battery charging
articles.summary: A joint Indian research team has developed a new organic framework (COF) material for sodium-ion battery electrodes. The material allows for rapid charging, reaching 80% capacity in 10 minutes, and offers a more sustainable and cost-effective alternative to lithium-ion batteries for large-scale energy storage and renewable energy integration.

articles.headline: NASA’s New Horizons spacecraft continues data collection from Kuiper Belt
articles.summary: NASA’s New Horizons probe, currently 9.5 billion km from Earth, has resumed its mission after a period of hibernation. The spacecraft is collecting data on the heliosphere and energetic particles as it moves toward the outer edges of the solar system, following its historic 2015 flyby of Pluto and subsequent exploration of the distant Kuiper Belt.

articles.headline: Researchers use AI to optimize sulphur-based energy storage systems
articles.summary: Scientists are using artificial intelligence to develop more efficient lithium-sulphur (Li-S) batteries. By identifying specific dual-atom catalysts that can better hold sulphur during charging cycles, the researchers aim to overcome the rapid degradation issues that have hindered the commercial use of high-capacity, low-cost sulphur batteries.

articles.headline: Tata Steel develops iron-fortified nutritional supplement from steel mill byproduct
articles.summary: In a novel circular economy initiative, Tata Steel has developed 'PiroNutri38', an iron-rich powder produced from the acid-washing process of steel sheets. The supplement is designed to tackle iron deficiency and has shown high bioavailability and consumer acceptance in initial sensory evaluations, offering a unique use for industrial byproducts.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu see diverging paths for greenfield airports
articles.summary: While Andhra's Bhogapuram airport is ready for inauguration, Tamil Nadu's Parandur airport project remains stalled by land acquisition hurdles and local protests. The contrast highlights the challenges of large infrastructure projects, where local opposition and environmental concerns can lead to significant delays in timelines and increased costs.

articles.headline: India focuses on demand-led port expansion and operational efficiency
articles.summary: India's maritime sector is shifting toward demand-driven port planning to ensure long-term sustainability. With a goal to reach 10,000 million tonnes of port handling capacity by 2047, the focus is on optimizing existing infrastructure, improving hinterland connectivity, and integrating digital tools for better cargo management and reduced costs.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh grants administrative nod for phase-II of three new ports
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has approved phase-II development for the Ramayapatnam, Mulapeta, and Machilipatnam ports. With an investment of over ₹1,638 crore, the expansion aims to increase the state's cargo-handling capacity from 195 million tonnes to 286 million tonnes per year, boosting maritime trade and industrial growth in the region.

articles.headline: Abra Group signs MoU to strengthen West Asia-Latin America aviation links
articles.summary: Abra Group, which owns Avianca and GOL, has signed a memorandum of understanding with Etihad Airways to enhance connectivity between Latin America and the Middle East. The partnership will focus on codesharing, frequent flyer programs, and cargo cooperation to expand the global reach of both airline networks and improve traveler options.

articles.headline: IATA advocates for standardized global methodology to calculate flight carbon emissions
articles.summary: The International Air Transport Association (IATA) is calling for a unified global approach to measuring CO2 emissions from flights. Currently, over 110 airlines use varying calculation methods, leading to inconsistent data for passengers. IATA aims to provide a more transparent and accurate way for travelers to track and manage their carbon footprint.

articles.headline: Healthcare workers remain vulnerable to violence years after RG Kar tragedy
articles.summary: Two years after the brutal attack at Kolkata's RG Kar Hospital, medical staff in India continue to face a rising tide of violence from patients' relatives. Despite demands for a Central Act to protect personnel and the creation of 'safe zones' in hospitals, little has changed in on-ground security, leaving doctors and nurses feeling unsafe and exposed.

articles.headline: Australia implements strict new restrictions on the sale of nicotine pouches
articles.summary: The Australian government has introduced new regulations to restrict access to nicotine pouches due to rising public health concerns. From July 24, these products can only be purchased through a pharmacy with a prescription, as health officials warn about the risks of nicotine addiction and harmful impacts on brain development in young people.

articles.headline: NFHS-6 report highlights persistent regional disparities in Indian healthcare
articles.summary: The sixth round of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) reveals that while India's total fertility rate has dipped below replacement level, significant regional gaps remain. States like Bihar and West Bengal continue to see high rates of early marriage, while female sterilization remains the dominant form of contraception across the country.

articles.headline: Proposed name change for PCOS aims to reflect complex hormonal nature
articles.summary: Experts are advocating for renaming Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) to 'poly metabolic ovary syndrome' to better reflect its status as a complex endocrine and metabolic condition. The change aims to validate women's concerns and reduce the stigma associated with the current diagnosis, which often focuses narrowly on fertility rather than overall health.

articles.headline: Global road crash deaths reach 1.16 million annually, says WHO
articles.summary: A new World Health Organization report reveals that road crashes claim 1.16 million lives globally each year. While there has been a slight decrease in overall death rates since 2011, the rise in motorcycle-related fatalities and risks to pedestrians remains a major concern, particularly in low and middle-income countries with rapid motorization.

articles.headline: World Hepatitis Day focuses on expanding access to life-saving care
articles.summary: On World Hepatitis Day, health organizations are calling for accelerated action to eliminate viral hepatitis by 2030. Despite the existence of effective vaccines and therapies, millions remain undiagnosed or unable to access treatment due to systemic inequalities and service gaps, particularly in underserved and rural populations.

articles.headline: India-US trade talks delayed pending Section 301 excess capacity investigations
articles.summary: Bilateral trade negotiations between India and the US are likely to see slow progress as the US concludes its Section 301 investigations into global excess capacity. The probe, covering sectors like steel and solar cells, could result in new trade measures that impact Indian exports, potentially complicating the broader trade partnership.

articles.headline: Rising memory prices push smartphones out of reach for budget consumers
articles.summary: Smartphone retailers in India are reporting a decline in footfall as rising memory component costs drive up the prices of entry-level and mid-range devices. Many consumers are delaying purchases or opting for refurbished phones, leading to concerns about a muted festive season for the mobile industry and a shift in consumer buying patterns.

articles.headline: CBDT issues detailed reporting norms for virtual digital asset transactions
articles.summary: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has released a 198-page document outlining detailed reporting requirements for crypto exchanges and intermediaries. While no new taxes have been introduced, the norms aim to tighten oversight and ensure transparency in the reporting of TDS on virtual digital asset transactions, bringing them into the formal tax net.

articles.headline: Supply chain issues lead to shortage of Old Monk rum in Maharashtra
articles.summary: Popular rum brand Old Monk has become increasingly difficult to find in Maharashtra due to supply chain disruptions. Retailers attribute the shortage to delays in bottling and dispatch at the distillery level, compounded by a spike in demand during the monsoon. The situation has forced many bars to stop serving the iconic spirit across the state.

articles.headline: Tata Consumer Products eyes double-digit growth through new-age portfolio
articles.summary: Tata Consumer Products Ltd (TCPL) aims to maintain its double-digit revenue growth by expanding its 'new-age' portfolio, which includes ready-to-drink beverages and health-focused snacks. CEO Sunil D’Souza stated that while traditional tea and salt businesses remain steady, future growth will be driven by innovation, premiumization, and digital integration.

articles.headline: Space for dissent in India is shrinking, warns SC Judge Bhuyan
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan warned that the space for dissent in India is shrinking as normal activities are increasingly criminalised. Delivering a lecture at the National Law Institute University, he questioned the disproportionate use of pellet guns and arrests for minor activities, citing cases where youths were denied bail for months for protests or social media posts.

articles.headline: Merchant vessel with four Indian nationals hit at Ukraine port
articles.summary: A merchant vessel carrying four Indian nationals was struck at Ukraine's Odesa port on Saturday. India's embassy in Ukraine confirmed that while two Indians are safe, the status of the other two remains unknown as search operations continue. The Ministry of External Affairs has issued an advisory warning Indian sailors to exercise extreme caution when operating in the Black Sea region.

articles.headline: CPCB red-flags green firecrackers over use of banned chemical barium
articles.summary: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has objected to the commercial production of new-generation 'green' firecrackers, alleging they still contain barium nitrate, a chemical banned by the Supreme Court. While CSIR-NEERI claims the formulations reduce emissions by 40-60%, the contradictory stands have left the final decision on their legality to the Supreme Court.

articles.headline: KPSC probes veterinary officer recruitment scam; selection list withheld
articles.summary: The Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) has formed an internal committee to investigate allegations of irregularities in the recruitment exam for veterinary officers. The decision follows media reports and a police case registered at Vidhana Soudha station. The final selection list has been withheld until the probe into suspected bribery and paper leaks is completed.

articles.headline: US FDA approves first oral pill to lower high cholesterol
articles.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Lipfendra (enlicitide), the world's first oral PCSK9 inhibitor to lower 'bad' cholesterol. The once-daily tablet provides a needle-free alternative to current cholesterol-lowering injections. While significant for patients with difficult-to-control cholesterol, the drug must undergo CDSCO approval before becoming available in India.

articles.headline: Tata Sons AGM faces quorum hurdle over Sir Ratan Tata Trust
articles.summary: The upcoming annual general meeting of Tata Sons faces a potential roadblock due to a quorum requirement in its articles of association. The Maharashtra charity commissioner has barred the Sir Ratan Tata Trust from holding board meetings, making it difficult to nominate a joint representative for the AGM. The meeting's agenda includes the reappointment of chairman N Chandrasekaran.

articles.headline: Child adoptions in India hit decade high with 5,022 cases
articles.summary: According to CARA data, 5,022 children were adopted in India between April 2025 and March 2026, the highest figure in over a decade. Over 2,700 of these adoptions were of girls. The agency also reported a 25% increase in the adoption of children with special needs. Despite the rise, nearly 26,000 prospective parents remain on the waiting list for available children.

articles.headline: Dinkwad couples and singles fuel Bengaluru's booming pet economy
articles.summary: Bengaluru is seeing a sharp rise in spending on pets, driven by young singles and 'Dinkwad' (Dual Income, No Kids, With A Dog) couples. Spending on specialised diets, grooming, and high-end boarding can range from Rs 3,000 to Rs 20,000 monthly. The shift has sparked growth in niche services like cat-only boarding and mobile grooming vans to cater to urban 'pet parents'.

articles.headline: Student athletes find success in balancing elite sports with academics
articles.summary: Several Bengaluru students have demonstrated success in balancing competitive sports with high academic achievement. Examples include Siddhant Vasan, a national table tennis player who secured an IIT Madras seat, and footballer Amrutha Kamath, who ranked fifth in the state PUC exams. Experts emphasize that discipline and time management allow students to excel in both fields.

articles.headline: Geotechnical dispute emerges over tilting 18-storey tower in Bengaluru
articles.summary: A conflict has emerged between developer SNN Raj Corp and Nagadi Consultants over the cause of a tilt in a tower at the SNN Raj Etternia complex. While the consultant claims its recommendation for pile foundations on the filled-up quarry site was ignored, the developer alleges the geotechnical report contained incorrect borehole data. The 49-unit tower is now set for demolition.

articles.headline: Bengaluru head constable suspended for taking Rs 5,000 bribe
articles.summary: A head constable at Pulakeshinagar traffic police station was suspended after a truck driver caught him on video accepting a Rs 5,000 bribe. The officer allegedly demanded the cash to release a vehicle booked for obstructing traffic, an offence for which only a magistrate can impose a penalty. The driver approached an activist with video evidence, leading to the suspension.

articles.headline: Dry summer triggers 311 million litre demand for Cauvery tankers
articles.summary: A severe dry spell in Bengaluru led to record bookings for the BWSSB's 'Cauvery On Wheels' service. Between May 2025 and July 2026, the utility supplied 311.8 million litres of water across 67,397 orders, generating over Rs 7 crore in revenue. Demand peaked in May, with apartment complexes in East Bengaluru accounting for nearly 60% of all bulk orders.

articles.headline: Silk Board junction gets facelift through volunteer beautification drive
articles.summary: Over 125 volunteers participated in a cleanup and beautification drive at Bengaluru's Silk Board junction. Organized under the Clean Bengaluru campaign, the drive involved repainting flyover pillars and constructing a new 100-metre-long footpath. The project, supported by Canadian firm CGI and NGO India Rising Trust, aimed to improve pedestrian safety at the chaotic transit hub.

articles.headline: Gen Z students pause Freedom Park protest but continue reform movement
articles.summary: Students and activists at Bengaluru's Freedom Park have formally paused their month-long demonstrations following the resignation of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan. However, organisers stressed that the movement has entered a new phase focused on structural education reforms, including fixing university governance and resuming student union elections in Karnataka.

articles.headline: Karnataka may scrap online transfer counselling for sub-registrars
articles.summary: The Karnataka government is considering a proposal to restore the old general transfer process for sub-registrars, just two months after introducing online counselling. A section of officials argued that digital counselling is 'unnecessary' and limits administrative discretion in high-revenue districts. Conversely, some officers support the system for reducing lobbying and corruption.

articles.headline: MLC CT Ravi refuses police notice over alleged provocative remarks
articles.summary: BJP MLC CT Ravi turned down a police notice regarding alleged provocative remarks targeting a community and protesters at Jantar Mantar. High drama occurred at his Chikkamagaluru residence as Ravi demanded a copy of the FIR and questioned the police's definitions of his speech. Supporters and BJP workers protested the police action, calling it a discriminatory move by the government.

articles.headline: Three Indian workers die in Gulf workplace accidents every week
articles.summary: Data from the Ministry of External Affairs reveals that over 800 Indian workers died in workplace accidents across the Gulf between 2023 and 2025, averaging three deaths per week. Saudi Arabia recorded the highest toll with 182 fatalities. Migrant associations attributed the high death rate to inadequate safety gear, extreme temperatures, and poor living conditions in labour camps.

articles.headline: Ration shop in Tamil Nadu transformed into community library hub
articles.summary: A fair price shop in Kolapakkam, Chengalpet, has been turned into a community hub featuring a library and reading corner. Shopkeeper Velu Chinnasamy, with support from local residents and a social worker, cleared the area and catalogued books ranging from school textbooks to literature. The initiative, named Thiruvalluvar Noolagam, now serves students, senior citizens, and women.

articles.headline: Uttarakhand professor debarred for life over BTech paper leak
articles.summary: Uttarakhand Technical University has debarred assistant professor Ashish Kumar Gupta from all academic work for life following his arrest in a paper leak case. Gupta, who was the paper setter, allegedly leaked two BTech Electronics exams, forcing the university to schedule re-tests for 377 students. He is currently in jail following a case registered by Dehradun police.

articles.headline: IT hiring in India stays muted despite surge in AI roles
articles.summary: While demand for Artificial Intelligence and machine-learning roles is growing, overall hiring in India's IT software industry remains cautious. Monthly hiring indices show a significant settle at levels lower than the 2021-22 peak. Software and services firms are adding far fewer people, suggesting that tech companies are maintaining a conservative approach to workforce expansion.

articles.headline: Infosys faces 175,000 Euro fine in France over labour compliance
articles.summary: French labour authorities have fined Infosys €175,000 (Rs 2 crore) for a non-compliant employee time-recording system. The regulator, DRIEETS, found shortcomings in the system's reliability and monitoring capabilities for certain staff categories. Infosys stated the penalty would have no material impact on its financial operations or business activities in the region.

articles.headline: BNP Paribas Cardif to acquire 26% stake in IndiaFirst Life Insurance
articles.summary: French insurer BNP Paribas Cardif has entered a definitive agreement to acquire a 26% stake in IndiaFirst Life Insurance from private equity firm Warburg Pincus. The deal will bring the French insurer into a partnership with Bank of Baroda and Union Bank of India. BNP Paribas Cardif aims to leverage its global bancassurance expertise to support the life insurer's next phase of growth.

articles.headline: July FPI inflows reach Rs 41,796 crore, breaking February record
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned net buyers in Indian equities in July, breaking a four-month selling streak. Cumulative inflows across equities and debt reached Rs 41,796 crore by July 24, surpassing the previous record set in February. The recovery was largely driven by primary market activity and sustained interest in Indian debt following global index inclusions.

articles.headline: Cyber frauds pivot to social engineering as technology hacks decline
articles.summary: India's cyber-fraud landscape is shifting from remote device takeovers to real-time social engineering. Fraudsters now use 'active call guidance' to manipulate victims into executing transactions themselves. A report by Biocatch shows detection of malware fell to 1.7% of sessions, while the value of attempted fraud payments rose 35%, supported by a vast network of 26.5 lakh mule accounts.

articles.headline: Bitchat app downloads surge in India despite government ban
articles.summary: The internet-free messaging app Bitchat, founded by Jack Dorsey, has seen a surge in India with over 65,000 downloads in a single week despite a government crackdown. The app allows messaging via Bluetooth mesh networks, bypassing internet shutdowns. India now accounts for 53% of Bitchat's global downloads, raising concerns about the effectiveness of unconstitutional digital restrictions.

articles.headline: UNESCO adds Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches to World Heritage
articles.summary: UNESCO has added several iconic sites to the World Heritage List, including Mount Olympus in Greece and the D-Day landing beaches in France. The committee also inscribed ancient Japanese capitals and South Sudan’s Boma-Badingilo Migratory Landscape. These sites were recognized for their cultural and natural significance, marking historical events and preserving unique biodiversity.

articles.headline: Chinese AI models gain popularity in US due to efficiency
articles.summary: American software developers and tech firms are increasingly adopting Chinese AI models like Moonshot’s Kimi and DeepSeek's V4. These models are gaining ground for being more affordable and efficient than US-based counterparts from OpenAI and Anthropic. Despite potential US sanctions and accusations of intellectual property theft, Chinese models now lead popularity rankings on global platforms.

articles.headline: Neeraj Chopra focuses on gold over 90-metre throw obsession
articles.summary: Double Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra stated he is not obsessed with the 90-metre mark, prioritizing consistency and major titles. Speaking ahead of the Commonwealth Games athletics events, he noted that difficult weather conditions often impact distances. Chopra emphasized that winning gold against elite competitors like Arshad Nadeem matters more than chasing a specific numerical record.

articles.headline: Sunil Chhetri signs one-year extension with Bengaluru FC
articles.summary: India's football icon Sunil Chhetri has signed a one-year contract extension with Bengaluru FC. The 41-year-old captain, who joined the club in 2013, has made a record 318 appearances and scored 134 goals. Chhetri stated that football and the club have given him everything, and he wanted to continue contributing as long as he felt he could help the team on the pitch.

articles.headline: Marvel casts David Jonsson as lead in Black Panther III
articles.summary: Marvel Studios officially announced Black Panther III at San Diego Comic-Con, confirming British actor David Jonsson will take on the lead role. Jonsson, known for the series 'Industry', will play the son of T’Challa, the character originally portrayed by the late Chadwick Boseman. The film is scheduled for a December 15, 2028, release, bringing fans back to the world of Wakanda.

articles.headline: NDC scraps provisional registration requirement for dental students
articles.summary: The National Dental Commission (NDC) has abolished the mandatory provisional registration from State Dental Councils for BDS graduates before starting their internships. The reform aims to save thousands of students from administrative delays and financial burdens. Graduates can now begin clinical training immediately after passing exams, accelerating their entry into the healthcare workforce.

articles.headline: AIBE pass rate falls to 65.9% as exam turns application-based
articles.summary: The pass percentage for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE XXI) dropped to 65.92% as the paper shifted from memory-based to scenario-based problems. Out of 1.75 lakh aspirants, only 1.15 lakh qualified. The Bar Council of India had to moderate the results by reducing the cut-off by three marks. Experts cited poor time management and new criminal codes as key factors for the decline.

articles.headline: CBSE Class X second board exam raises overall pass to 96.7%
articles.summary: The first edition of the CBSE Class X second board examination has helped raise the overall pass percentage to 96.78%. Over 6.64 lakh students registered for the second exam to improve scores or clear compartments. The 'best of two' provision and additional preparation time reduced student stress, with significant improvements noted in Science and Mathematics results.

articles.headline: Pune Porsche Crash: Police Arrest Grandfather For Wrongful Confinement Of Driver
articles.summary: Pune police have arrested the grandfather of the 17-year-old involved in the Porsche crash for allegedly kidnapping and confining the family's driver to force him into taking responsibility for the accident. The investigation also revealed a blood-sample swapping conspiracy involving Sassoon General Hospital doctors to conceal the minor's alcohol intake at the time of the fatal crash.

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court Scraps OBC Certificates Issued In West Bengal Since 2010
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court cancelled nearly 5 lakh OBC certificates issued in West Bengal after 2010, citing procedural illegalities. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee stated she would not accept the "politically motivated" order. Prime Minister Modi welcomed the ruling, accusing the Trinamool Congress of using quotas for communal appeasement and vote-bank politics.

articles.headline: RBI Approves Record Dividend Payout Of Rs 2.11 Lakh Crore To Government
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has approved a record-high dividend of Rs 2.11 lakh crore to the central government for the fiscal year ending March 2024. This 141% increase from the previous year is expected to provide significant fiscal relief, allowing the government to manage its deficit and increase capital expenditure on infrastructure projects across the country.

articles.headline: Campaigning Peak For Phase 6 Of Lok Sabha Elections In Delhi constituencies
articles.summary: High-octane campaigning concluded for Phase 6 of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections across 58 constituencies, including all seven seats in Delhi and 10 in Haryana. Key leaders from the BJP and the INDIA bloc held mega rallies and roadshows, focusing on issues of constitutional rights, unemployment, and national security. Voting is scheduled to take place this Saturday.

articles.headline: Swati Maliwal Assault Case: Delhi Court Rejects Bibhav Kumar's Bail Plea
articles.summary: A Delhi court dismissed the bail application of Bibhav Kumar, aide to CM Arvind Kejriwal, in the Swati Maliwal assault case. The court observed that the allegations are serious and there is a possibility of tampering with evidence or influencing witnesses given the accused's position. Maliwal alleged she was brutally assaulted inside the Chief Minister's official residence.

articles.headline: UGC To Allow Biannual University Admissions From 2024-25 Academic Year
articles.summary: The University Grants Commission announced that universities in India can now offer admissions twice a year, in July-August and January-February. This flexibility aims to help students who miss the summer cycle and will allow universities to increase their enrollment capacity. The move is aligned with the National Education Policy 2020 goal of internationalizing higher education.

articles.headline: Severe Heatwave Grips Northern India As Temperatures Cross 47 Degrees Celsius
articles.summary: The IMD has issued a red alert for Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan as a severe heatwave continues. Several stations recorded temperatures exceeding 47°C. Authorities have advised citizens to avoid outdoor exposure during peak hours and have extended school holidays to protect children from heat-related illnesses and dehydration during the peak summer period.

articles.headline: IMD Forecasts Cyclone Remal Formation In The Bay Of Bengal Region
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department warned of a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal, likely to intensify into Cyclone Remal by Sunday. The storm is expected to make landfall between West Bengal and Bangladesh. Coastal districts have been put on high alert, and fishermen are advised to return to shore as heavy rainfall and strong winds are predicted for the weekend.

articles.headline: ICJ Orders Israel To Stop Military Offensive In Rafah Immediately
articles.summary: In a landmark ruling, the International Court of Justice ordered Israel to halt its military operations in Rafah, Gaza, citing immense risk to the Palestinian population. The court also ordered the opening of the Rafah crossing for humanitarian aid. While Israel rejected the ruling as biased, it faces increased diplomatic isolation and pressure from the international community.

articles.headline: China Conducts Massive Military Drills Encircling Taiwan As Strong Punishment
articles.summary: The Chinese military launched two days of massive war games around Taiwan, describing them as punishment for separatist acts following the inauguration of President Lai Ching-te. The drills involve the navy, air force, and rocket forces, simulating a full-scale blockade and precision strikes on key targets. Taiwan has condemned the drills as irrational provocations.

articles.headline: Indian Stock Markets Surge To Record Highs Following RBI Dividend Announcement
articles.summary: Domestic equity benchmarks Nifty 50 and Sensex hit all-time highs following the RBI's announcement of a record dividend payout. Investor sentiment was bolstered by the prospect of reduced government borrowing and improved fiscal health. Financial and infrastructure stocks led the rally, with the Nifty crossing the 22,900 mark during intraday trade on Thursday.

articles.headline: Adani Energy Solutions Receives Approval To Raise Rs 12,500 Crore
articles.summary: Adani Energy Solutions has received board approval to raise up to Rs 12,500 crore through the issuance of shares to institutional investors. The funds are earmarked for expanding the company’s transmission network and smart metering business. This marks the group's most significant return to the equity market for capital raising since early 2023.

articles.headline: Dedicated Freight Corridor Completes 90 Percent Of Western Section Construction
articles.summary: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India announced that 90% of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor is now complete. The project aims to decongest the existing rail network and reduce the transit time of goods between Mumbai and Delhi. The final section is expected to be commissioned by the end of the current fiscal year, boosting logistics efficiency.

articles.headline: IPL 2024: Sunrisers Hyderabad Face Rajasthan Royals In High Stakes Qualifier 2
articles.summary: Sunrisers Hyderabad and Rajasthan Royals are set to clash in the second qualifier of IPL 2024 at Chennai's M.A. Chidambaram Stadium. The winner will qualify for the final against Kolkata Knight Riders. SRH looks to leverage its aggressive batting lineup, while RR hopes to capitalize on its balanced bowling attack in spin-friendly conditions.

articles.headline: Cannes Film Festival: Indian Documentary 'Sunflowers Were The First Ones' Wins
articles.summary: Indian filmmaker Chidananda Naik's documentary, 'Sunflowers Were the First Ones to Know', won the La Cinef First Prize at the 77th Cannes Film Festival. The film, based on a Kannada folk tale, was praised for its visual storytelling. This victory highlights the growing influence of Indian regional cinema and student filmmakers on the prestigious global stage.

articles.headline: Health Ministry Issues Advisory On Rising H5N1 Avian Influenza Cases Globally
articles.summary: Following reports of H5N1 avian influenza cases in several regions, the Union Health Ministry has issued a fresh advisory to state governments. The guidelines emphasize poultry surveillance, the use of personal protective equipment by handlers, and public awareness about symptoms. While the risk to humans in India remains low, authorities are taking preemptive measures.

articles.headline: ISRO Successfully Completes Crucial Test For Gaganyaan Service Module Propulsion
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully conducted the final hot test of the Gaganyaan Service Module Propulsion System. The test validated the performance of the liquid engines in simulated space conditions. This milestone brings India closer to its goal of launching its first crewed space mission, which is currently planned for late 2025.

articles.headline: August Rush: Over 2 Dozen Cos Plan IPO Debut Next Month
articles.summary: Over 24 companies are planning to launch their initial public offerings in August, aiming to raise a collective ₹35,000 crore. High-profile startups and firms like Zepto, PhonePe, and Shiprocket are expected to lead the pipeline. This surge follows a strong recovery in market sentiment and aims to capitalize on improved domestic institutional flows despite global uncertainties.

articles.headline: UAE Eyes Ties in Critical Minerals, Wider Air Service Pact
articles.summary: The UAE and India are exploring a strategic partnership in the critical minerals sector to secure supply chains for renewable energy and electric vehicles. UAE Minister of Economy Abdulla Bin Touq Al Marri also called for a revision of bilateral air service agreements to increase seat capacity, aiming to support the next phase of economic cooperation and tourism growth between the nations.

articles.headline: Bain Capital Set to Buy Stake in IndusInd General Insurance
articles.summary: Private equity major Bain Capital is in advanced talks to acquire up to a 25% stake in IndusInd General Insurance. The deal could value the insurer at approximately ₹16,000 crore. The acquisition would mark Bain's first major entry into India's general insurance sector and follows Hinduja Group's efforts to divest a portion of its insurance arm for strategic capital infusion.

articles.headline: Corrosion Costs India ₹14 Lakh Crore Annually, Power Sector Worst Hit
articles.summary: A report by Nomura and the Bureau of Indian Standards estimates that corrosion-induced damage costs India approximately ₹14 lakh crore per year, or 4.3% of its GDP. The power sector is the most severely affected, accounting for ₹38,320 crore in losses. The study emphasizes the urgent need for better protective measures and adherence to global standards to prevent infrastructure decay.

articles.headline: Mutual Funds Flag High Zepto Valuation for Upcoming IPO
articles.summary: Top domestic mutual funds have expressed concerns over the $4-5 billion valuation sought by Zepto for its proposed IPO. Funds are reportedly pushing for a 30-40% discount, citing the hyper-competitive nature of the quick commerce market and recent volatility in new-age tech stocks. Zepto aims to raise nearly ₹8,010 crore through the listing to fund its aggressive expansion plans.

articles.headline: Protium in Advanced Talks to Buy Clix Capital
articles.summary: Protium Finance is in late-stage negotiations to acquire fellow non-banking financial company Clix Capital in a deal valued between ₹1,900-2,200 crore. The merger would combine Protium's retail lending strength with Clix's established MSME portfolio. The deal is expected to conclude by August, helping Protium scale its operations and diversify its asset base in the credit market.

articles.headline: Private Equity Firms Shun Legacy IT Companies for AI Startups
articles.summary: Global PE investors are shifting focus from traditional IT services firms to AI-native startups. Data shows that AI startups captured 59% of software deal value in the first half of 2024. Investors are wary of high-cost legacy models and are instead backing platforms that automate business workflows. This pivot reflects a fundamental change in the software investment landscape.

articles.headline: Infosys Loses Three Mega IT Deals to Aggressive Rivals
articles.summary: Infosys has lost three major multi-million dollar contracts to competitors as rivals offer deeper price cuts to win market share. The losses come amidst intense competition for large IT budgets. Analysts suggest that while Infosys is prioritizing profit margins, aggressive bidding by peers like HCLTech is successfully luring long-term clients seeking maximum cost savings.

articles.headline: More Indian-Made EVs Head to Europe and Southeast Asia
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki and Tata Motors are ramping up exports of locally produced electric vehicles to international markets, including Europe and Southeast Asia. Maruti Suzuki recently shipped its first batch of electric SUVs to Europe. The move aims to capitalize on the growing global demand for affordable electric mobility and offset potential domestic slowdowns through global sales.

articles.headline: Brands Foresee Strong Festive Demand Despite Global Economic Headwinds
articles.summary: Consumer brands in India are anticipating robust sales during the upcoming festive season, driven by strong demand in rural and semi-urban markets. Retailers are planning aggressive marketing campaigns to attract customers. While global headwinds remain a concern, industry experts believe that high consumer sentiment and new product launches will lead to double-digit growth this year.

articles.headline: Rupee Near Record Low, Faces Pressure from Rising Oil Prices
articles.summary: The Indian rupee is trading near its all-time low of 83.97 against the US dollar, pressured by rising global crude oil prices and continued capital outflows. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia are further weighing on investor sentiment. Analysts expect the Reserve Bank of India to intervene to prevent excessive volatility as the currency tests the psychological 84-per-dollar mark.

articles.headline: Finance Minister Rules Out Adjusting Budget Estimates for Now
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that the government is not planning to revise its budget estimates despite global economic uncertainties. She emphasized that India has sufficient buffers to manage external shocks, including volatile energy prices. The FM highlighted that domestic tax collections remain strong, providing fiscal space to maintain planned infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: Opposition Leaders Seek to Continue Attacks on Police Action
articles.summary: Opposition parties in India are planning to intensify their protests against alleged police high-handedness during recent demonstrations. Leaders have called for a judicial probe into incidents of violence and the use of excessive force. They claim that the government is using law enforcement to suppress democratic dissent, while the ruling party defends the actions as necessary.

articles.headline: India Reaches Atmanirbhar Milestones in Defense and Space Technology
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi lauded India's progress toward self-reliance in the defense and space sectors during his 'Mann Ki Baat' address. He highlighted the successful testing of indigenous missiles and the growth of private space startups. The PM emphasized that 'Vocal for Local' is becoming a reality, with over 75% of materials used in many new defense systems being locally sourced.

articles.headline: Hailing Youth, Uddhav Thackeray Says Struggle is Just Beginning
articles.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackeray addressed a gathering of young supporters, stating that their recent protests are just the start of a larger movement. He praised the youth for challenging the current administration on issues like exam leaks and unemployment. Thackeray called for unity among opposition forces to protect democratic institutions and constitutional values in India.

articles.headline: Gen Z Turns Instagram Into a New Political Public Square
articles.summary: Instagram has emerged as a primary platform for political discourse among Gen Z in India. Young activists are using Reels and Stories to organize protests and share information on social issues. Data shows that posts related to student rights and exam reforms have garnered over 300 million views, forcing political leaders to engage more actively with the platform to reach young voters.

articles.headline: OIC Urged to Intervene Over Alleged Human Rights Abuses in PoJK
articles.summary: Human rights groups have written to the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the UNHRC, alleging systematic human rights violations by Pakistani authorities in PoJK. The letters cite excessive use of force, arbitrary arrests, and the suppression of free speech during recent public protests. Activists are calling for an independent international probe into the reports from the region.

articles.headline: India Gears Up for Month-Long Summit Diplomacy Focusing on Global South
articles.summary: India is preparing for a series of high-level diplomatic meetings, including the SCO and G20 summits, with a focus on representing the interests of the Global South. Prime Minister Modi is expected to advocate for reforms in global financial institutions and stronger cooperation on climate change. The diplomatic push aims to solidify India's position as a leading voice for developing nations.

articles.headline: Punjab Police Arrest Key Operative of ISI-Backed BKI Module
articles.summary: The Punjab Police have arrested a high-ranking operative of an ISI-backed Babbar Khalsa International (BKI) terror module. The arrest led to the recovery of sophisticated weapons and explosive devices intended for targeted killings. Officials stated that the module was being handled by handlers based in Pakistan and aimed to disturb the peace and communal harmony in the border state.

articles.headline: Army Seeks Indigenous Drone Radars for Counter-Terror Operations
articles.summary: The Indian Army is looking to procure indigenously developed drone-mounted radars to enhance its counter-terrorism capabilities in Jammu and Kashmir. These radars are designed to detect movement through dense foliage and underground tunnels used by terrorists. The project, under the 'Make-II' category, aims to reduce reliance on imports and support the domestic defense manufacturing industry.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Farmers Urge CM to Reject Mekedatu Talks Invitation
articles.summary: Farmer associations in Tamil Nadu have urged Chief Minister M.K. Stalin to reject Karnataka's invitation for talks on the Mekedatu dam project. They argue that the project would violate previous water-sharing agreements and harm the interests of farmers in the Cauvery delta. The groups are calling on the state government to maintain its firm opposition and seek a legal resolution.

articles.headline: India's National AI Mission Scales Up with 27 New Labs
articles.summary: India's National AI Mission has reached a new milestone with 27 operational labs now live across 21 states. The project aims to train over 5,000 students in AI and data science to meet the growing industry demand. The government plans to add another 188 labs in the coming months, focusing on ITIs and polytechnics to provide hands-on technical training to students in smaller cities.

articles.headline: Foxconn Signals Shift to High-Value Manufacturing in India
articles.summary: Foxconn is planning to expand its Indian operations beyond smartphone assembly into high-value manufacturing segments like semiconductors and EV components. The company cited India's improving infrastructure and favorable policy environment as key drivers for this shift. This move is expected to create thousands of high-skilled jobs and integrate India more deeply into global supply chains.

articles.headline: IITs Launch Specialised Cybersecurity Degrees to Bridge Talent Gap
articles.summary: Several Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) are launching specialized degree programs in cybersecurity to address a projected shortage of 1.5 million professionals in the field. The courses will focus on areas like network security, threat intelligence, and digital forensics. Industry experts welcomed the move, noting that specialized training is crucial to defend against complex cyberattacks.

articles.headline: DeepSeek AI Pauses Fundraising Amid Global Market Volatility
articles.summary: Beijing-based AI startup DeepSeek has put its latest $1 billion fundraising round on hold, citing global market volatility and shifting investor interest. The company was expected to reach a multi-billion dollar valuation. The pause reflects a broader trend of cooling interest in late-stage AI startups as investors demand clearer paths to profitability and sustainable business models.

articles.headline: Meta Withdraws from Global Clean Energy Pact Over Cost Concerns
articles.summary: Meta has announced its withdrawal from a major international clean energy pact, citing the rising costs of renewable energy certificates. The company stated that while it remains committed to its sustainability goals, the current structure of the pact is no longer economically viable. The decision has drawn criticism from environmental groups who argue it sets a poor example for other tech firms.

articles.headline: Anthropic Partners with SK Hynix for Custom AI Chips
articles.summary: AI research firm Anthropic has signed a deal with South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix to develop custom semiconductors for its large language models. The partnership aims to optimize hardware performance for AI training and reduce reliance on mainstream providers like Nvidia. The custom chips are expected to significantly lower operational costs and improve the speed of Anthropic's AI services.

articles.headline: Michelin-Starred Chef Faces Charges Over Insect-Based Recipes
articles.summary: A Michelin-starred chef in South Korea is facing legal action for allegedly using non-approved insects as ingredients in a high-end tasting menu. While the chef argues that the insects are safe and sustainable, local health authorities maintain that they are not on the list of approved food items. The case has sparked a debate over food safety regulations and the future of alternative proteins.

articles.headline: Higher Steel Prices Impact Costs of Household Utensils
articles.summary: Manufacturers of kitchenware and stainless steel utensils are raising prices by up to 7% due to a surge in global steel costs. Input costs for nickel and iron ore have risen sharply in the last quarter, forcing firms to pass the burden to consumers. Industry experts predict that demand may remain muted in the short term as households cut back on non-essential durable goods purchases.

articles.headline: Crypto Platforms Must Share User Data with I-T Department Annually
articles.summary: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued new guidelines requiring cryptocurrency platforms to share comprehensive user transaction data with the Income Tax department every year. The move aims to curb tax evasion and bring more transparency to the digital asset market. Platforms failing to comply could face stiff penalties and the suspension of their operating licenses in India.

articles.headline: Cabinet to Approve Incentive Scheme for Construction Equipment Manufacturing
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet is set to approve a new production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for the manufacturing of heavy construction and mining equipment. The ₹12,000-crore scheme aims to boost domestic production and reduce reliance on imports from China. This initiative is part of the government's broader 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' strategy to strengthen India's industrial manufacturing base.

articles.headline: Tax Filers Rush to Disclose Foreign Assets Before July 31
articles.summary: Indian taxpayers are scrambling to disclose their foreign assets and bank accounts ahead of the July 31 income tax return deadline. The I-T department has sent over 2 lakh alerts to individuals with mismatched data in their Annual Information Statements. Failure to accurately report foreign holdings can lead to heavy penalties and prosecution under the Black Money Act.

articles.headline: Sebi Proposes New PMS Framework for Mass Affluent Investors
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has proposed a new 'MF-Only' Portfolio Management Service (PMS) category with a lower entry barrier of ₹25 lakh. Currently, the minimum investment for PMS is ₹50 lakh. The new framework aims to provide retail investors with access to professional wealth management services while maintaining strict transparency and risk management norms.

articles.headline: Credit Card Issuance in India Hits Two-Year High in June
articles.summary: Credit card issuance in India saw its highest monthly growth in over two years this June, with banks adding 1.14 million new cards. Total cards-in-force reached 121.5 million, reflecting strong consumer confidence and a shift toward digital payments. HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank led the growth, despite stricter regulatory norms on unsecured lending introduced by the RBI earlier this year.

articles.headline: Maruti Suzuki Shifts Focus to SUVs to Drive Future Sales
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki is realigning its product strategy to focus heavily on the SUV segment, aiming to capture over 25% market share in the category by 2026. The carmaker plans to launch five new SUV models over the next two years. This shift reflects changing consumer preferences in India, where SUVs now account for nearly half of all passenger vehicle sales, surpassing hatchbacks.

articles.headline: Large Occupiers Drive Strong Demand in India’s Office Market
articles.summary: Demand for Grade-A office space in India's top eight cities grew by 15% in the first half of 2024, driven by large occupiers and Global Capability Centres (GCCs). Bengaluru and Delhi-NCR remained the top markets for leasing activity. Experts attribute the growth to the return-to-office trend and India's growing importance as a global hub for tech and professional services.

articles.headline: French Firm Forvia to Invest €70 Million in Indian Auto Parts
articles.summary: French automotive supplier Forvia has announced a fresh investment of €70 million to set up three new manufacturing plants in India by 2030. The company aims to double its Indian revenue to €1 billion as it taps into the growing domestic demand for premium auto components and EV parts. The new facilities will focus on sustainable materials and advanced electronics for global carmakers.

articles.headline: Air India to Modify Boeing 787 Fleet Following FAA Directive
articles.summary: Air India will modify several Boeing 787 Dreamliners in its fleet following a safety directive from the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The directive requires inspections and potential repairs of doorway components to prevent malfunctions. The airline stated that the modifications will be carried out during scheduled maintenance to minimize disruptions to its international flight schedule.

articles.headline: Temporary Calm as Iran-Israel Tensions Enter a Brief Pause
articles.summary: Tensions in West Asia have entered a period of temporary calm as both Iran and Israel appear to be avoiding further immediate military escalation. Diplomatic efforts by the US and regional powers are focused on preventing a full-scale regional war. However, analysts warn that the situation remains extremely fragile, with both sides maintaining a high state of military readiness.

articles.headline: Israel Kills Top Hamas Official in Targeted Strike in Gaza
articles.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that a targeted airstrike in Gaza killed a high-ranking Hamas official responsible for weapons procurement. The strike is part of Israel's ongoing campaign to dismantle the group's leadership structure. Hamas has vowed to retaliate, raising fears of a renewed surge in violence. International observers are calling for a ceasefire to protect civilian lives.

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine Trade Heavy Missile and Drone Fire
articles.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged intense missile and drone strikes over the weekend, targeting critical infrastructure and military positions. Ukraine reported significant damage to its energy grid, while Russia claimed to have intercepted dozens of drones over its border regions. The escalation comes as both sides prepare for new offensives, with no signs of peace negotiations in sight.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy Claims Russia Seeking 30,000 More North Korean Troops
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has claimed that Russia is seeking to recruit an additional 30,000 troops from North Korea to bolster its frontline forces. This follows reports of North Korean engineers already operating in occupied territories. Zelenskyy urged Western allies to increase military aid, stating that the involvement of foreign troops marks a dangerous escalation in the war.

articles.headline: China Probes Death of Child in Illegal Gene-Editing Trial
articles.summary: Chinese authorities have launched an investigation into the death of a young girl during an unauthorized gene-editing trial at a private clinic. The trial aimed to cure a rare genetic disorder but reportedly lacked proper ethical approvals and safety protocols. The case has reignited global concerns over the lack of regulation in the field and the potential for 'designer baby' experiments.

articles.headline: Wildfires Rage Across France and Spain Amid Heatwave
articles.summary: Thousands of people have been evacuated as erratic wildfires continue to rage across southern France and parts of Spain. Firefighters are struggling to contain the blazes due to high temperatures and strong winds.
