Local authorities have declared a state of emergency in the most affected regions, and several European nations have sent firefighting aircraft to assist in the rescue operations.

articles.headline: Philippines, Japan, and US Complete Joint Naval Drills
articles.summary: The naval forces of the Philippines, Japan, and the United States have completed a series of joint drills in the South China Sea. The exercises focused on maritime security, search and rescue, and anti-submarine warfare. The drills aim to promote a 'free and open Indo-Pacific' amidst rising territorial tensions with China, which has condemned the maneuvers as provocative.

articles.headline: Student groups aim to carry Jantar Mantar momentum into DUSU polls
articles.summary: As the Jantar Mantar protest ends, student organizations like AISA and NSUI are preparing to shift their campaign to Delhi University campuses, aiming to leverage the momentum and issues raised during the 36-day agitation for the upcoming Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) polls.

articles.headline: Outstation students lament fewer holiday spells in DU this year
articles.summary: Outstation students at Delhi University are finding it difficult to plan trips home due to fewer holiday spells in the new academic calendar. Major festival breaks, like Deepavali and Navratri, have been significantly reduced, impacting their travel and family time.

articles.headline: DU extends deadline for candidates to accept seats
articles.summary: The University of Delhi (DU) on Sunday extended the deadline for candidates allotted seats in the second round of undergraduate admissions to accept their offers. Colleges have been asked to verify and approve applications promptly.

articles.headline: Former East Delhi Mayor Nirmal Jain appointed Delhi Minorities Commission chief
articles.summary: Former East Delhi Mayor Nirmal Jain was appointed Chairperson of the Delhi Minorities Commission by Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta. Mr. Jain is the first non-Muslim to head the commission since its constitution in 2000.

articles.headline: 46% Delhi schools have safety deficiencies
articles.summary: Nearly 46% of 1,677 schools inspected in Delhi were found to have safety deficiencies under the 'Student Safety Checklist,' with 774 schools flagged for gaps. Private schools accounted for the highest share of these deficiencies, prompting corrective action.

articles.headline: Shivakumar to convene MPs’ meet in Delhi on State issues
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has called a meeting of all Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha members from Karnataka in New Delhi on Monday. The meeting aims to discuss the State's pending proposals before the Centre and seek bipartisan support during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.

articles.headline: Jeevan Jyoti vision centres strengthen rural eye care in Alwar
articles.summary: New vision centres established at government health facilities in rural Alwar district, Rajasthan, under the Jeevan Jyoti Project, have significantly strengthened eye care services. These centres provide screening, refraction, cataract referrals, and free near-vision glasses, increasing footfall for eye care.

articles.headline: Sitting MLAs among Kerala leaders facing sexual abuse charges
articles.summary: Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader M.C. Kamaruddin, with around 120 pending cases, tops the list of Kerala people's representatives facing criminal proceedings. Five people's representatives, including sitting MLAs, are reportedly facing sexual harassment charges.

articles.headline: Revanth to speak to Rahul over opening doors of Parliament, Assembly to Gen Z
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will discuss with Rahul Gandhi a proposal to lower the age for entry into the Legislature to 21. Reddy aims to channel the energies of Gen Z by giving them more political opportunities and will seek support from INDIA bloc partners.

articles.headline: U.P. CM takes on SP in Etawah, Mainpuri; reaches out to youth
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath attacked the Samajwadi Party (SP) in its strongholds of Etawah and Mainpuri, inaugurating development projects worth over ₹1,200 crore. He accused the previous SP government of nepotism and tarnishing the district’s image.

articles.headline: Take note of ‘irregularities’ in JPSC exam, Champai urges HC
articles.summary: BJP leader Champai Soren urged the High Court to take suo motu cognisance of alleged irregularities in Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission examinations. He demanded a CBI probe into all recruitment processes conducted by the two panels.

articles.headline: Dipke sparked revolution, must get security, says Sena Minister
articles.summary: Maharashtra Minister and Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Shirsat expressed pride that Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), sparked a revolution and deserved security. Shirsat visited Dipke’s family and called for security for the activist, who is yet to return home.

articles.headline: Palaniswami, ex-AIADMK MLAs to appear before Speaker on July 30
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker J.C.D. Prabhakar has summoned AIADMK general secretary and party floor leader Edappadi K. Palaniswami, along with four former party MLAs, to appear before him on July 30. They face disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.

articles.headline: Not shifting to national politics, says Fadnavis
articles.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis dismissed speculation about shifting to national politics after a quick trip to Delhi, reaffirming his focus on Maharashtra. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Eknath Shinde claimed the Opposition attempted to use students' protests to create unrest.

articles.headline: Bengal CM meets kin of victims of Sundarbans trawler capsize
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari met families of the Sundarbans trawler capsize victims, announcing ₹5 lakh ex gratia and a civic volunteer job for one eligible member. He also pledged efficient officers for coastal police stations to improve disaster management.

articles.headline: Eroding identities of Brahmaputra’s children
articles.summary: Government-issued records are failing citizenship tests before Foreigners Tribunals and the Gauhati High Court in Assam. This SPOTLIGHT article details cases like Aminul Hoque's, where minor discrepancies in names, ages, and shifting residences led to individuals being declared foreigners, highlighting systemic issues.

articles.headline: A missing link and Lifelong Learning can
articles.summary: India's doctoral research ecosystem in Social Sciences urgently needs structural overhaul. The current system is plagued by mandatory publication, exploitation by supervisors, and administrative delays. The article advocates for research to connect to societal and real-world issues, making academia-society links mandatory for relevance and impact.

articles.headline: Raman Kant Munjal Scholarships
articles.summary: The Raman Kant Munjal Foundation offers scholarships ranging from ₹40,000 to ₹550,000 annually for three years. Eligibility: Indian nationals in the first year of BBA, BFIA, B.Com. (H, E), BMS, IPM, B.A. (Economics), BBS, or any other Finance-related degree, with academic merit and family income criteria. Deadline: August 31.

articles.headline: ICPC Internship
articles.summary: The Policy, Politics and Governance Foundation offers an internship for students in their final or penultimate year of graduation interested in a career in political or policy strategy consultation. Rewards: ₹5,000 a month and certificate. Application: Online. Deadline: Round the year.

articles.headline: Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Fund Scholarship for Doctoral Studies
articles.summary: The Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Fund offers scholarships for full-time Ph.D. scholars below 35 years as of October 1, registered to a recognised Indian institution, with a first-class postgraduate degree (at least 60% aggregate). Rewards: Up to ₹18,000 a month and benefits. Deadline: August 31.

articles.headline: IELTS update
articles.summary: IDP Education announced that IELTS in India will transition from IELTS on Paper to IELTS on Computer from September 2026. Candidates can choose between 'IELTS on Computer' (all sections on computer) or 'IELTS on Computer (Writing on Paper)' (Writing on paper). Speaking tests remain face-to-face.

articles.headline: Youth at the vanguard
articles.summary: The resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, following sustained youth agitation over exam paper leaks, marks a seminal moment against the BJP-dominant party system. Protesters, leveraging social media and non-violent resistance, forced the government's hand, highlighting the power of a vigilant civil society against state brutality and unyielding institutions.

articles.headline: Do not surrender to China, do not depend on the U.S.
articles.summary: This opinion piece argues against India's economic appeasement with China, citing a decade of unprovoked hostility and Beijing's unipolar ambitions. It warns against relying on the unpredictable U.S. and advocates strategic patience, internal strengthening, supply chain resilience, and diversified trade partnerships to counter China's structural challenge without unilateral disarmament.

articles.headline: The youth have risen against authoritarianism
articles.summary: The author praises the youth-led protests, especially over the NEET debacle, as a triumph against authoritarianism. The Education Minister's resignation, compelled by a disciplined movement, is hailed as a 'positive development' demonstrating that people, when united, can hold power accountable and reclaim democratic space from an overbearing government.

articles.headline: Indian Monsoon: a democratic tipping point
articles.summary: This article posits that large student demonstrations and Sonam Wangchuk's fast signify India's democratic tipping point, where citizens demand to be heard and shape their future. It calls for a new national agenda, focusing on constitutional values, scientific temper, and human dignity, to build a more inclusive, equitable, and innovative society for the next generation, especially in the age of AI.

articles.headline: A gamble on the Cauvery issue
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's decision to initiate direct talks with Karnataka on the Cauvery water dispute departs from the State's traditional policy of preferring adjudication. While some disapprove of bypassing established mechanisms like CWMA, Mr. Vijay may be leveraging his ties with Karnataka's ruling Congress party for a breakthrough.

articles.headline: Need to shift focus to rising student suicides, cost of education
articles.summary: While protests over NEET paper leaks led to a Minister's resignation, systemic issues persist. Over 1.23 lakh students died by suicide between 2014-2024, with 'failure in examination' accounting for over one-fifth. High coaching costs and intense competition in exams like NEET exacerbate stress, highlighting the need for broader reforms beyond paper leaks.

articles.headline: Why is China’s AI push gaining ground?
articles.summary: Despite U.S. chip restrictions, Chinese firms like Moonshot AI and DeepSeek are rapidly advancing in AI, releasing open-weight and open-source models downloaded millions of times. China leverages abundant electricity and less advanced chips. Beijing's support for domestic champions and restrictions on foreign co-option have fostered a competitive AI ecosystem, aiming to move from digital to physical world applications.

articles.headline: Why India has moved to take down BitChat repositories?
articles.summary: India's Cyber Crime Coordination Centre directed GitHub to remove BitChat repositories, citing the Bluetooth mesh messaging app's anonymous communication and potential for unlawful assembly, surveillance evasion, and incitement of cognizable offences. The Internet Freedom Foundation criticized the order for relying on potential misuse rather than identifying unlawful content, arguing it violates proportionality standards.

articles.headline: Why India must modernise the way govt. publishes laws and regulations
articles.summary: India's fragmented, PDF-dependent legal publishing system impedes access to laws for citizens, lawyers, and courts. The article highlights how sections of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2005, were never notified. It advocates adopting open legal publishing standards like Akoma Ntoso, used by other countries, to enhance transparency, democratic participation, and make laws accessible.

articles.headline: She was dialled in during the presentation
articles.summary: This 'Know Your English' column explains the phrase 'dialled in,' which means being very focused on a task, deriving from tuning old radios to avoid static. It also clarifies 'becomes you' to mean something suits a person, often used for compliments or commenting on behavior.

articles.headline: How well do you know Vincent van Gogh, one of history’s most celebrated and influential artists?
articles.summary: This daily quiz challenges readers with questions about Vincent van Gogh, covering his iconic painting 'The Starry Night,' his fellow artist Paul Gauguin, his influence from Japanese woodblock prints, his profession before art, and the French village where he died.

articles.headline: Odisha BJP leaders criticise post by MP’s daughter on Pradhan
articles.summary: A social media post by BJP MP Aparajita Sarangi’s daughter, Archita Sachin Rahar, celebrating Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation as Union Education Minister, sparked resentment within Odisha BJP ranks. Party leaders criticised Ms. Rahar, stating Mr. Pradhan is a "son of the soil" and her remarks hurt Odias.

articles.headline: Assam CM plays down Minister’s daughter joining CJP protest in Guwahati
articles.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma downplayed his Cabinet Minister Keshab Mahanta's daughter joining a Cockroach Janta Party protest against NEET irregularities. Sarma stated that the actions of adult children should not be linked to their parents' political ideology, though he disagreed with her slogans.

articles.headline: M.P. man booked on Pradhan
articles.summary: A social media content creator, Yashpal Soni, has been booked in Madhya Pradesh’s Niwari district for allegedly using "highly abusive" language. The charges relate to a video clip he posted targeting former Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the BJP, and the Delhi Police amid student agitation.

articles.headline: ‘Pradhan had offered to quit at start of protest’
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh Cabinet Minister Kailash Vijayvargiya claimed Dharmendra Pradhan offered to resign as Union Education Minister at the very beginning of the NEET paper leak protests but was asked by the party leadership to wait. Vijayvargiya alleged Pradhan’s resignation "foiled plans of foreign forces" to create unrest.

articles.headline: ‘Foreign extremists’ behind violence in Kolkata: Bengal CM
articles.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari claimed that "Islamic fundamentalists," possibly with foreign backing, were behind the violence during NEET protests in Kolkata on Friday. He announced 14 arrests and stated that multiple FIRs were lodged against actor Sreelekha Mitra for an "objectionable cartoon" poster.

articles.headline: News Analysis: The reframing of the political narrative by Gen Z
articles.summary: The NEET protests, spearheaded by Gen Z and activist Sonam Wangchuk, challenged the government's 'all is well' narrative, evolving beyond education reform into a broader expression of youth anxiety. The movement, which bypassed mainstream media, highlighted a new political force and poses a significant challenge for the BJP to regain youth trust.

articles.headline: Sonam Wangchuk to be discharged from hospital today; will visit Rajghat
articles.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk will be discharged from Medanta Hospital in Gurugram on Monday. He plans to visit Rajghat to pay homage to Mahatma Gandhi before leaving for Ladakh, after breaking his 26-day hunger strike, which was part of the agitation against alleged NEET irregularities.

articles.headline: Students are more important than any post: Home Minister
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated that for the BJP, the nation, its youth, and students are far more important than any position. He affirmed the Modi government's respect for student sentiments and its commitment to implementing reforms against paper leaks, praising Dharmendra Pradhan's efforts despite his resignation.

articles.headline: A day later, traces of protest removed from Jantar Mantar
articles.summary: New Delhi Municipal Corporation (NDMC) officials conducted a major cleanliness and beautification drive at Jantar Mantar, removing posters and covering graffiti. The extensive operation, involving over 500 officers and employees, aimed to restore public spaces a day after the 36-day agitation concluded.

articles.headline: At Mumbai rally, people happy with Pradhan’s exit, but slam govt. on E20
articles.summary: A rally in Mumbai celebrated Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, but protesters, including Gen Z and millennials, also expressed dissatisfaction with the government over the implementation of E20 (ethanol-blended petrol). They raised concerns about its impact on vehicles, mileage, and the affordability of pure petrol.

articles.headline: Hunger strike was challenge to govt., the movement is still on, says AISA secretary
articles.summary: Neha, Delhi secretary of AISA, stated that their hunger strike at Jantar Mantar was a "challenge to the government," aiming to force action, not self-sacrifice. She viewed Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as only the first step and asserted that the broader movement to reclaim democratic space continues.

articles.headline: RSS women’s wing seeks uniform policy on population
articles.summary: The Rashtra Sevika Samiti, the women’s parallel of the RSS, adopted a resolution expressing concern over "population imbalance" in India. The resolution urged the Centre and State governments to formulate a uniform national population policy applicable to all communities to address demographic changes impacting the country's identity.

articles.headline: Youth have decisive role in shaping the future of India: Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged India's youth to play a decisive role in national development, expressing confidence in their ability to shape the country's future. He highlighted programs like Viksit Bharat Dialogue and the Viksit Vibrant Village Programme, which engage young people with rural and border village realities, broadening their understanding and commitment.

articles.headline: 3 Great Indian Bustard chicks placed in rewilding tunnel
articles.summary: In a first, three endangered Great Indian Bustard chicks have been moved into a custom-built rewilding tunnel at the Godawan Conservation Centre in Jaisalmer. This ₹9.25-crore facility aims to prepare captive-bred birds for life in the wild by minimizing human contact and mimicking their natural habitat.

articles.headline: Life lessons from Ramayana
articles.summary: This article highlights the Ramayana as a treatise on life, educating and elevating mental and spiritual well-being. It showcases devotion, dharma, and the ideal family, imparting unique lessons on right conduct and family dynamics, such as Rama's immediate acceptance of banishment to honor his father's word.

articles.headline: Sold your car? Ensure ownership transfer
articles.summary: This article advises car sellers on the critical importance of ensuring vehicle ownership transfer is completed to avoid legal liabilities for accidents or court summons. It recommends signing Forms 29 and 30 with buyer details, retaining copies, and sending a disclaimer letter to the RTO via Speed Post with proof of delivery.

articles.headline: How passionate are you about your collectibles?
articles.summary: This article explores passion assets like paintings and antiques, which offer both consumption and investment value. It discusses the 'pain premium' that makes owners reluctant to sell and advises documenting provenance, age, acquisition details, and ensuring proper preservation to enhance the assets' value for eventual sale.

articles.headline: What’s behind the vault
articles.summary: This article explains the lifecycle of an Electronic Gold Receipt (EGR) in India's gold exchange, from the physical gold deposit with vault managers to its conversion into tradeable EGRs by depositories. It details how EGRs represent fungible gold, allowing investors to take physical delivery from any eligible vault, ensuring quality and transparency.

articles.headline: New U.K. PM vows to put ‘Britain’s interest first’ in ties with Trump
articles.summary: U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated he would "put Britain’s interest first" when dealing with U.S. President Donald Trump and would be willing to challenge him if needed. This declaration came in excerpts from a BBC interview released on Sunday.

articles.headline: Cuban leader accuses Washington Trump of seeking to ‘appropriate’ island
articles.summary: Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel on Sunday denounced Washington’s pressure campaign against his country as a "genocidal policy." He accused the U.S. of seeking to "appropriate" the island, stating that the decades-long embargo and oil blockade are "weapons of war" causing deaths.

articles.headline: Trump is giving Iran talks ‘some space’; no munition issue: Waltz
articles.summary: U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz stated on Sunday that President Donald Trump is giving negotiations with Iran "some space." He dismissed reports that Washington was rationing munitions over supply concerns, affirming that the U.S. remained "locked and loaded" for more attacks.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques in West Bank following deadly clashes
articles.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank on Sunday, setting fire to two mosques and scrawling graffiti, including "Jewish revenge," on buildings. This followed Friday's deadly clashes that killed four Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers near Nablus.

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine report civilian deaths as attacks intensify
articles.summary: Russian and Ukrainian strikes on Sunday killed at least 10 people, with Kyiv reporting an attack on a supermarket in northern Ukraine and Russia accusing Kyiv of striking a bus stop in occupied Gorlivka. Both sides reported civilian casualties as attacks intensified across the frontline.

articles.headline: Netanyahu fires back at Mamdani and calls ICC charge ‘bogus’
articles.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu accused New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani of "fomenting hate" for calling the Israeli Prime Minister a war criminal and advocating for his arrest. Netanyahu dismissed the International Criminal Court’s war crimes charges against him as "bogus," asserting his intent to address the UN General Assembly.

articles.headline: Gymnast Langton discharged from hospital after a nasty fall
articles.summary: England’s Gabriel Langton was discharged from hospital after scans revealed no lasting damage from a fall during the Commonwealth Games men’s team final in Glasgow. Langton landed awkwardly off the high bar, temporarily halting the competition for 20 minutes.

articles.headline: ‘The young bunch of players have been showing tremendous energy’
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer described his maiden T20I series win as skipper as a "special moment." He praised his young team for their "tremendous energy" on the field, noting that such enthusiasm is exactly what he requires as a captain.

articles.headline: Hodge, Hope help West Indies post 311 in the first innings
articles.summary: Skipper Shai Hope's 92 and a knock of 84 by Kavem Hodge helped West Indies make 311 in the first innings against Pakistan on the second day of the first Test at Tarouba. Mohammed Ali took 4/50 for Pakistan.

articles.headline: Neeraj delighted to be back at CWG where it all began
articles.summary: Olympic gold medallist Neeraj Chopra expressed his delight returning to the Commonwealth Games, where his senior career began in 2018. The javelin thrower, who missed the 2022 edition due to injury, stated he has worked on his fitness and technique, feeling much better now for the upcoming event.

articles.headline: Sooryavanshi sparkles in India’s clean sweep against Zimbabwe
articles.summary: Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored a quickfire 81, leading India to a 35-run victory over Zimbabwe on Sunday. This win completed a 3-0 Twenty20 International series sweep for India at the Harare Sports Club, with Zimbabwe managing 157/7 in reply to India's 192/5.

articles.headline: U Mumba’s UTT reign continues
articles.summary: Defending champion U Mumba TT snapped Dempo Goa Challengers’ unbeaten run with an 8-5 victory to retain the Ultimate Table Tennis crown in the Season-7 final. Meanwhile, Raynier Fernandes scored a hat-trick to power Jamshedpur FC to a 5-0 crushing win over Sri Lankan Armed Forces side Defenders FC in the Durand Cup.

articles.headline: Indian men bag youth Asian title, women settle for silver
articles.summary: The Indian sub-junior men’s hockey team defeated Pakistan 3-1 to win the gold medal at the FIH Youth Hockey5s Asian Championship in Muscat. In the women’s competition, India settled for silver after a 2-4 loss in the final against China.

articles.headline: Kush Maini finishes second in Hungary
articles.summary: Kush Maini secured his third podium finish of the 2026 season by coming in second in Sunday’s FIA Formula 2 feature race at the Hungaroring in Hungary. This achievement adds to his consistent performance this season.

articles.headline: Raynier’s hat-trick powers Jamshedpur to easy win
articles.summary: Debutant Raynier Fernandes scored a brilliant hat-trick, leading Jamshedpur FC to a dominant 5-0 victory over the Sri Lankan Armed Forces side Defenders FC in their Group C clash at the Birsa Munda Football Stadium in Ranchi, marking a strong start to their Durand Cup campaign.

articles.headline: AITA rejects panel’s proposal to have five SOM in EC
articles.summary: The All India Tennis Association (AITA) rejected the Justice (Retd.) Gita Mittal-led panel’s recommendation to have five Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) in its 15-member Executive Committee. The AITA instead opted to have two SOMs and four women in the EC, aligning with the National Sports Governance Act.

articles.headline: Delhi’s Doseja ready for the second season syndrome
articles.summary: Young Delhi cricketer Dhruv Doseja, who had a conversation with former India opener Wasim Jaffer on the 'second season syndrome,' is preparing to perform in the third season of the Delhi Premier League, which starts on July 31.

articles.headline: One N Only should make amends
articles.summary: The five-year-old gelding One N Only, who ran second in his last start, should make amends in the Anab E Shahi Trophy (1,400M), the main event at Hyderabad, with App. A. Asbar riding for trainer James Mckeown.

articles.headline: Alfonsine wins the main event
articles.summary: Alfonsine (A. Imran Khan) won the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Memorial Trophy, the main event at Hyderabad, by a neck. The horse, owned by Mr. S.N. Harish, was trained by M. Srinivas Reddy.

articles.headline: Cricket’s summer of goodbyes
articles.summary: The summer of 2026 witnessed a wave of retirements from international cricket by numerous stars, including Sophie Devine, Suzie Bates, Lea Tahuhu, Kane Williamson, Ben Stokes, Heather Knight, and Tammy Beaumont. This period also marked the end of high-profile coaching stints for Brendon McCullum and Stephen Fleming, signifying a significant generational shift in the sport.

articles.headline: India’s first dengue vaccine arrives with a crucial safety caveat
articles.summary: India's drug regulator approved Qdenga, its first dengue vaccine, but clinical trial data raise a crucial safety caveat. The vaccine may enhance dengue in seronegative children if exposed to DENV-3, which it doesn't adequately protect against. Researchers recommend screening for prior dengue exposure before vaccination to avoid potential Antibody-Dependent Enhancement (ADE).

articles.headline: PRAXIS: grazing planet rings
articles.summary: NASA selected 'PRAXIS' (Planetary Rings Autonomous EXploration with In-situ Sampling) for phase I funding. This mission concept involves a bio-inspired robotic explorer, driven by AI, capable of directly sampling particles from planetary ring systems without collision. It aims to answer open questions about how planetary rings form, evolve, and their composition.

articles.headline: Pralhad Joshi takes charge as education minister amid protests
articles.summary: Pralhad Joshi assumed charge as Education Minister amidst protests over exam paper leaks. His immediate task is to rebuild trust and address structural challenges in the education system.

articles.headline: NBS SUDOKU #4950
articles.summary: A Sudoku puzzle to be solved.

articles.headline: PSBs cash in on gold loan boom, sell PSLCs
articles.summary: Public sector banks earned healthy income by selling Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs), boosted by growing gold loan portfolios. IOB's fee income surged significantly.

articles.headline: US pharma tariffs a wake-up call for Indian industry
articles.summary: Experts believe proposed US tariffs on generic drugs are a wake-up call for Indian pharma to diversify markets and boost innovation, noting details remain unclear.

articles.headline: Court ruling on commercial services under consumer law
articles.summary: A consumer complaint was dismissed as the National Commission deemed disputes involving commercial transactions not maintainable under the Consumer Protection Act.

articles.headline: Catch the scam if you can: Bank frauds expose governance
articles.summary: Bank frauds, often orchestrated by syndicates exploiting depositor trust and digital vulnerabilities, highlight governance gaps. Recoveries remain low, and accountability is diluted.

articles.headline: India’s digital trade dilemma: Stakes high as WTO moratorium lapses
articles.summary: India faces a strategic dilemma as the WTO moratorium on e-transmission duties lapses, impacting digital trade and potentially increasing costs and uncertainty for Indian firms.

articles.headline: Mobile phone exports thrive; value addition lags
articles.summary: India's mobile production growth is driven by exports, but value addition lags due to high component imports. Dependence on imported components persists.

articles.headline: Market shifts in favour of high-growth, quality stocks: PGIM India MF
articles.summary: PGIM India MF notes a market shift towards high-quality, high-growth stocks, which have outperformed significantly in FY27, reversing previous trends.

articles.headline: ‘Dramatic rally elusive, but healthy returns within reach’
articles.summary: BNP Paribas predicts healthy double-digit returns for Indian equities driven by easing foreign outflows, reasonable valuations, and earnings growth, despite moderate rally expectations.

articles.headline: United Spirits’ growth lifted by premium mix despite volume dip
articles.summary: United Spirits saw revenue growth driven by the P&A segment, despite volume declines in the popular segment due to policy changes. The company remains positive on sector recovery.

articles.headline: Oil, West Asia crisis, US Fed rate decision to drive markets
articles.summary: West Asia conflict, oil prices, and the US Fed's rate decision will be key drivers for markets this week, alongside corporate earnings, analysts said.

articles.headline: One dozen firms set for market debut next month
articles.summary: Over a dozen companies, including Zepto and Truhome Finance, are expected to launch IPOs next month, collectively raising ~25,000 crore amid improving market sentiment.

articles.headline: Suzlon Energy asks SAT for relief against Sebi penalty
articles.summary: Suzlon Energy's management has approached the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) challenging a Sebi penalty for alleged lapses in financial statement disclosures.

articles.headline: Beyond CJP, beyond Delhi: How movement took on a life of its own
articles.summary: The student protest movement for exam reforms decentralized, spreading across India powered by students, satire, and shared outrage, evolving beyond its initial organizers.

articles.headline: Income tax notice: Respond with facts and documents, not panic
articles.summary: Taxpayers receiving income tax notices should verify them on the portal, respond promptly with supporting documents, and file revised returns if needed to avoid penalties.

articles.headline: Indigenous 350kg turbojet engine a milestone for Pvt defence tech
articles.summary: India's first indigenous 350kg thrust turbojet engine, developed by GTRE and manufactured by Azad Engineering, marks a critical step in mastering complex aerospace propulsion technology.

articles.headline: Gujarat floods: Death toll touches 35; 790 evacuated
articles.summary: Gujarat floods have claimed 35 lives, with 790 people evacuated. Rescue operations are ongoing in affected districts like Valsad and Navsari, while the situation in Assam improved.

articles.headline: Nirav Modi still here: UK shadow minister 'appalled'
articles.summary: A UK shadow minister expressed horror that fugitive jeweler Nirav Modi remains in the UK despite a prima facie case for extradition, criticizing Britain's response.

articles.headline: Reorienting PDS: Move from food security to nutrition security
articles.summary: India's PDS needs to shift from ensuring calorie intake to improving nutrition, with coverage potentially reduced based on affordability data, and savings reinvested in nutrient-rich foods.

articles.headline: 1991 reforms trusted mkts; now RBI should trust exporters
articles.summary: Sunil Bharti Mittal reflects on 1991 reforms, calling them a 'ticket to heaven', and advises that the RBI should now trust exporters and importers with simplified regulations.

articles.headline: The invisible heist: How some bank staff exploit depositors
articles.summary: Bank employees exploit depositor trust through organized fraud schemes involving fictitious loans, forged documents, and inter-branch coordination, highlighting governance gaps and the need for better oversight.

articles.headline: US presses Mexico to mirror its steel tariff wall
articles.summary: The US urges Mexico to impose tariffs on non-North American steel and aluminum imports to preserve preferential treatment for regional producers, as part of USMCA talks.

articles.headline: Maldives prez prepared to help facilitate Saarc revival
articles.summary: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu is ready to facilitate the resumption of Saarc meetings, which have been stalled for nine years, recognizing its importance as a regional organization.

articles.headline: Brazil denies visas to US officials over upcoming elections
articles.summary: Brazil's Foreign Ministry denied visas to two US State Department officials seeking to observe upcoming elections, escalating political tensions between the two nations.

articles.headline: CAG flags WBIDC’s ~12.86 cr loss in land deal with Flipkart unit
articles.summary: A CAG report flagged a ~12.86 crore loss for WBIDC in a land deal with Flipkart's logistics arm due to incorrect base price calculation, omitting water bodies.

articles.headline: DeepSeek said to tell backers of funding pause after viral posts
articles.summary: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek has reportedly suspended its second fundraising round after comments by its founder about US-China AI competition went viral.

articles.headline: Sateliot eyes India market, incorporates local subsidiary
articles.summary: European satellite operator Sateliot, specializing in IoT connectivity, eyes the Indian market and has incorporated a local subsidiary to tap growth opportunities.

articles.headline: Tax authority releases detailed guidance for service providers
articles.summary: CBDT issued a 198-page guidance note for Crypto-Asset Service Providers (RCASPs) to comply with reporting obligations under the IT Act, 2025, aligning with OECD's CARF framework.

articles.headline: ONGC starts drilling India’s first deepwater well off Odisha coast
articles.summary: ONGC began drilling its first deepwater exploratory well in the Mahanadi offshore basin off Odisha, aiming to unlock hydrocarbon potential and reduce import dependence.

articles.headline: NGT seeks Centre response on damage to Bihar oxbow lake
articles.summary: The National Green Tribunal has sought a response from the Centre on the deteriorating ecological condition of Asia's largest oxbow lake in Bihar, Kanwar lake.

articles.headline: Paradip Petrochemical Complex: Odisha begins land acquisition
articles.summary: Odisha commenced land acquisition for IOC's ~61,077 crore Paradip Petrochemical Complex, set to be one of India's largest petrochemical hubs.

articles.headline: ‘1991 Budget speech was Freedom Day for us; world was open’
articles.summary: Sunil Bharti Mittal recalls the 1991 reforms as 'Freedom Day' that transformed India's telecom sector, enabling Bharti Enterprises' growth. He emphasizes the need for continued reforms.

articles.headline: Lodha Developers targets 20% profit growth citing improved demand
articles.summary: Lodha Developers targets 20% net profit growth in FY27, projecting ~4,100 crore on improved housing demand and project execution, with Q1 profit doubling.

articles.headline: Air India modifying certain Dreamliners for door assist handle issue
articles.summary: Air India is modifying some Boeing 787 planes to address a door assist handle issue identified by the FAA, ensuring passenger and crew safety.

articles.headline: Allied Blenders targets mid-teen revenue growth in FY27
articles.summary: Alco-beverage firm Allied Blenders expects mid-teen revenue growth in FY27 driven by premiumization, exports, and capacity expansion, maintaining stable EBITDA margins.

articles.headline: Costa Coffee store count shrinks to 198 in India in FY26
articles.summary: Costa Coffee's store count in India decreased to 198 in FY26 from 220, marking the first decline in over five years, as per its franchise partner Devyani International.

articles.headline: Maruti Suzuki eyes 900,000 units of CNG vehicle sales in FY27
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki aims to sell 900,000 CNG vehicles in FY27, a 30% increase, driven by rising demand post-West Asia war, impacting sales from small cars to SUVs.

articles.headline: PM Sets Up Task Force Led by Nilekani for Exam Reforms
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has formed a high-powered task force chaired by Nandan Nilekani to overhaul the National Testing Agency (NTA). The panel will recommend technological and structural reforms to prevent paper leaks and ensure transparency in public examinations. The move aims to address recent controversies and protect students' interests through more secure testing processes.

articles.headline: Mirabai Chanu secures golden hat-trick at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
articles.summary: Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu won her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold in the women's 48kg event, lifting a total of 190kg. She set a new Games record with an 85kg snatch and 105kg clean & jerk. Fellow Manipuri lifter Rishikanta Singh secured a silver medal in the men's 60kg category with a total lift of 264kg, equalling the snatch record despite a knee injury.

articles.headline: US and Iran halt attacks amid renewed truce efforts
articles.summary: The United States and Iran have paused direct military strikes for a second day as diplomatic efforts to secure an interim ceasefire continue. The pause follows a period of heightened tensions sparked by drone attacks on merchant ships and retaliatory strikes. Officials from both countries expressed a desire to return to the terms of a ceasefire deal originally signed in June.

articles.headline: Siddaramaiah Blames Money Power, Rules Out Contesting 2028 Polls
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announced he will not contest the 2028 Assembly elections, citing the increasing influence of 'money power' in politics. He expressed concerns that the cost of elections is undermining democratic principles and making it difficult for honest candidates to compete. Siddaramaiah stated he will remain active in public life but will focus on mentoring youth.

articles.headline: Noida sewage tank fumes kill two cleaning workers
articles.summary: Two workers died after inhaling toxic fumes while cleaning a sewage treatment plant tank at a residential society in Noida's Sector 150. The victims were employees of a private contractor. Police have registered a FIR against the society's management and the contractor for negligence and failure to provide safety gear to the workers during the hazardous task.

articles.headline: Tadej Pogacar wins record-equaling fifth Tour de France title
articles.summary: Slovenian cyclist Tadej Pogacar secured his fifth Tour de France title with a dominant performance in the final stage in Paris. Pogacar joins an elite group of riders with five Tour victories, including Eddy Merckx and Bernard Hinault. He finished over six minutes ahead of defending champion Jonas Vingegaard, after winning five individual stages during the grueling three-week race.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi asks Home Minister about 'lethal force' on students
articles.summary: Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi wrote to Home Minister Amit Shah questioning the use of 'lethal force' and tear gas against students protesting over the NEET exam leak. Gandhi alleged that several students were injured during a police crackdown at Jantar Mantar and demanded accountability for the 'barbaric' police action. He called for a peaceful dialogue to resolve the issues of the student community.

articles.headline: Iran vows revenge after Ukraine drone hits ship in Caspian Sea
articles.summary: Iran's foreign ministry has warned of a 'deadly response' after a Ukrainian drone reportedly hit an Iranian merchant vessel in the Caspian Sea. Tehran accused Kyiv of violating international law by targeting non-military cargo ships. This incident marks an expansion of the conflict into new regions and has raised concerns about the safety of commercial shipping in the Caspian Sea.

articles.headline: India sweeps T20I series against Zimbabwe with 35-run win
articles.summary: India defeated Zimbabwe by 35 runs in the third T20I at Harare to clinch the three-match series 3-0. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was the standout performer, scoring a quickfire 81 off 49 balls to help India reach 191/5. In response, Zimbabwe was restricted to 156/7 as Indian bowlers, led by Mayank Yadav's three-wicket haul, maintained tight control throughout the innings.

articles.headline: Lando Norris Wins Hungarian Grand Prix as McLaren Dominates
articles.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris secured a commanding victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix, leading a one-two finish for the team. Norris's win marks a significant boost in the constructors' championship battle against Red Bull. Defending champion Max Verstappen finished third after a difficult race. The result highlights McLaren's rapid technical improvements and their emergence as a consistent threat.

articles.headline: Inflation remains RBI's foremost priority, says Governor Shaktikanta Das
articles.summary: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das stated that curbing inflation remains the central bank's top priority despite global risks. He noted that the Monetary Policy Committee will maintain a data-dependent approach to bring inflation within the 4% target. Das also highlighted plans to attract foreign capital, targeting $32 billion in inflows via FCNR(B) deposits to strengthen the rupee.

articles.headline: PM Narendra Modi taps Nandan Nilekani to lead exam reforms panel
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a high-powered task force led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to overhaul India's examination system. The panel, which includes former ISRO chief S Somanath, aims to develop tech-driven, leak-proof frameworks following recent paper leaks. It will focus on structural changes within the National Testing Agency to ensure transparency and integrity.

articles.headline: Nepal ends decade-long ban on high-denomination Indian currency notes
articles.summary: The Nepal Rastra Bank has lifted a nearly 10-year restriction, allowing Indian and Nepalese nationals to carry Indian currency notes of Rs 200 and Rs 500 denominations. Travellers can carry up to Rs 25,000 per person. The restriction was originally implemented following India's 2016 demonetisation. The move aims to facilitate trade and tourism for Indian and Nepalese nationals.

articles.headline: Berlin Pride Attack Investigated as Possible Act of Extremism
articles.summary: German police are investigating an attack on a Berlin Pride event as a potential act of Islamic extremism. One person was killed and several others injured when a suspect drove a vehicle into the crowd. The suspect, who was arrested at the scene, reportedly had links to radical groups. The incident has led to increased security at public events across Germany and sparked national outrage.

articles.headline: Siddaramaiah announces retirement from electoral politics after current term
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has declared he will not contest the 2028 assembly elections, citing his age and health. Speaking in Mandya, the 79-year-old leader stated that politics has become too corrupt and it is time for him to step down. He will have completed 50 years in politics by 2028 and intends to complete his current tenure as MLA before retiring.

articles.headline: Assam flood toll rises to 66 as four more deaths reported
articles.summary: The death toll from floods in Assam has reached 66 after four more fatalities were reported in the last 24 hours. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma stated that with four people still missing, the final toll could reach 75. Disaster management authorities are continuing rescue operations as rains persist across the state, affecting thousands of residents.

articles.headline: FSSAI Suspends Westend Agro Products Licence Over Quality Violations
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has suspended the manufacturing license of Westend Agro Products due to multiple quality violations. Inspections revealed the use of substandard ingredients and poor hygiene practices at their facilities. The regulator has ordered a recall of all current stock and warned that failure to comply will lead to permanent cancellation.

articles.headline: Wildfires force 300,000 to flee across France and Spain
articles.summary: Unpredictable wildfires have overwhelmed firefighters in southwestern France and parts of Spain, forcing over 300,000 people to evacuate. In France, the city of Bordeaux is under threat, while major highways and train lines have been cut. Spanish authorities are battling new fronts near Madrid and Valencia. Interior ministers described the situation as a 'historic' and 'unfavourable' disaster.

articles.headline: Anahat Singh becomes first Indian to win World Junior Squash title
articles.summary: 18-year-old Anahat Singh scripted history by becoming the first Indian to be crowned World Junior Squash champion. She defeated Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 3-0 in the final held in Canada, ending Egypt's 13-year dominance in the girls' category. The top seed and world No. 20 on the senior tour described the landmark victory as a dream after several years of finishing in the late rounds.

articles.headline: Washington Sundar ruled out of first Test against Sri Lanka
articles.summary: India's Test squad preparations for the Sri Lanka tour have been hit by injuries, with all-rounder Washington Sundar ruled out of the first Test due to a hamstring injury. Pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah and batter Sai Sudharsan are also subject to fitness tests. Harshit Rana and Nitish Kumar Reddy have also been ruled out, complicating the selection process for the two-Test series.

articles.headline: Any Dialogue With Pak Would Solely Focus On PoK: Rajnath
articles.summary: Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that any future talks with Pakistan will focus exclusively on Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). Speaking at a Kargil Vijay Diwas event, he emphasized that PoK is an integral part of India. He also criticized Pakistan for sponsoring a 'terror ecosystem' while India builds a 'startup ecosystem,' ruling out dialogue on other terms.

articles.headline: IDFC First Bank Expects to Maintain Profit Growth in FY27
articles.summary: IDFC First Bank expects its quarterly profitability to stay consistent through FY27, driven by falling credit costs and a lower cost of funds. MD & CEO V Vaidyanathan stated that the bank's digital-first strategy and focus on retail deposits are yielding results. The bank is also leveraging AI to manage its portfolio and maintain asset quality across diverse loan segments.

articles.headline: China’s CXMT Makes Historic Debut Amid Global Memory Frenzy
articles.summary: Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT saw its shares surge by 150% on its first day of trading in Shanghai. The historic debut comes as global demand for DRAM and HBM chips reaches record highs, driven by the AI boom. CXMT is China's best hope for achieving self-sufficiency in the semiconductor sector, and its successful listing is seen as a major win for Beijing's tech ambitions.

articles.headline: Centre warns Indians about jobs in Black Sea
articles.summary: The MEA reiterated its advisory for Indian seafarers to carefully assess security risks in the volatile Black Sea. This follows an incident where a projectile hit the MV AGN Ragnar near Odesa, with four Indian nationals on board; two are safe, and information on the other two is awaited amid ongoing search operations.

articles.headline: Not a single paper leak in Punjab: CM amid Oppn. attack
articles.summary: Fending off criticism from Opposition parties regarding "paper leaks" in poll-bound Punjab, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann stated that not a single case of paper leak has come to light during the Aam Aadmi Party government's four-and-a-half-year tenure.

articles.headline: BJP using unfair campaign practices ahead of Bankipur bypoll, says Kishor
articles.summary: Prashant Kishor accused the BJP of using unfair campaign practices ahead of the Bankipur bypoll, alleging the deployment of 'Jeevika Didis' for campaigning and harassment of his party leaders by the district administration. He threatened a sit-in protest if these practices are not stopped within 24 hours.

articles.headline: Tejashwi demands release of protesters held in Bihar
articles.summary: Bihar Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav demanded the immediate release of students, Opposition MLAs, and other protesters, including his elder brother Tej Pratap Yadav, who were arrested during Saturday's Bihar Bandh. He warned of a massive agitation if they are not released within 24 hours.

articles.headline: Mirabai makes it a golden day for India; Rishikanta clinches a silver
articles.summary: Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu secured her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in the women's 48kg category, setting new Games records. Earlier, Rishikanta Singh Chanambam clinched a silver medal in the men's 60kg category, making it a golden opening day for India in weightlifting.

articles.headline: Iran says it is halting ‘retaliatory strikes’
articles.summary: Iran announced a halt to its "retaliatory operations" in West Asia after the U.S. paused strikes. This follows Iran's claims of a tanker explosion in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran also reported progress in talks with Oman on "common principles and operational mechanisms" for ships in the Strait.

articles.headline: India scaling new heights in defence production: PM
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Mann Ki Baat address, stated that India is continuously strengthening its technological capabilities, defence production, and exports. He cited the induction of INS Mahendragiri, successful missile tests, and remarkable achievements by Indian sportspersons and science Olympiad students as examples of national pride.

articles.headline: Developers rethink IPO plans as housing market cools
articles.summary: Several real estate firms are rethinking IPO plans due to weaker housing demand and a cautious investment climate. Companies are shelving or pushing back listing timelines amid a slowdown in sales and muted sentiment.

articles.headline: Electric car race widens as new entrants gain traction
articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki, VinFast, and Tesla captured 8.1% of India's e-PV market in H1CY26, accounting for 18% of incremental registrations. New entrants are expanding the market rather than just taking volumes from incumbents.

articles.headline: ME advises seafarers to assess conflict risks
articles.summary: India has urged citizens to carefully assess security situations before accepting jobs on commercial vessels in conflict zones, particularly the Black Sea, following attacks on ships carrying Indians.

articles.headline: 2W makers ride export wave, but watch road ahead
articles.summary: Indian two-wheeler makers are cautiously optimistic about exports amid global uncertainty, with Hero, TVS, and Bajaj achieving export milestones. They remain watchful of geopolitical tensions, inflation, and supply chain disruptions.

articles.headline: Hindustan Zinc planning ~25K cr capex to expand capacity
articles.summary: Hindustan Zinc plans ~25,000 crore capex to expand refined metals capacity, including a new zinc smelter. The company aims to increase capacity 1.7 times to 2,000 ktpa by FY30.

articles.headline: TVS ILP plans up to ~2,700 cr capex to grow warehousing
articles.summary: TVS ILP plans ~2,500-2,700 crore capex over three years to expand warehousing from 12 msf to 20 msf by 2028, focusing on eastern and central India and Tier-II/III cities.

articles.headline: Tata Tech confident of a ‘breakout year’ in FY27
articles.summary: Tata Technologies expects a breakout year in FY27 driven by accelerated investment from auto manufacturers in new products. The company has won several full vehicle development projects.

articles.headline: House panel moots SMC Bill reset, tighter criminal provisions
articles.summary: Parliamentary Committee on Finance backs revisions to SMC Bill, including a preamble revision, limits on criminal provisions, and notice for probes. It suggested dropping a controversial clause for declaring new offenses.

articles.headline: UPI-linked PF claim roll out now in August
articles.summary: EPFO's UPI-linked PF claim settlement rollout delayed to August due to glitches on its CITES 2.01 platform. Login failures and slow processing have been reported by members.

articles.headline: Bank of Baroda aims $3 bn in FCNR (B) deposits
articles.summary: Bank of Baroda expects RoA above 1% in remaining FY27 quarters despite a $600 million litigation settlement. It targets $3 bn in FCNR(B) deposits and $1 bn in ECB/OFCB.

articles.headline: Oil near $100 puts Fed, peers in rate spotlight
articles.summary: Central bankers globally will reveal concerns about oil near $100/barrel and energy-driven inflation. Investor bets point to potential September rate hikes, though immediate action is not predicted.

articles.headline: Will call out Trump if required: UK’s Burnham
articles.summary: UK's new PM Andy Burnham stated he will 'always put Britain's interests first' and is willing to call out US President Trump if necessary, prioritizing national interest.

articles.headline: Australian PM to raise concerns over new tariffs with US Prez
articles.summary: Australian PM Anthony Albanese will raise US tariffs on Australian goods with President Trump, calling them unjustified and seeking their removal amidst concerns over forced labor allegations.

articles.headline: Meet the woman who stands to inherit much of Epstein’s fortune
articles.summary: Dentist Karyna Shuliak, Epstein's girlfriend, may inherit up to $100 million from his estate. Investigative files reveal Epstein helped her with US citizenship and managed properties.

articles.headline: US tariff move a wake-up call for Indian pharma, say experts
articles.summary: Proposed US tariffs on generic medicines are a wake-up call for Indian pharma to diversify exports, reduce single-market dependence, and accelerate innovation, experts say.
